expected: First feasible run: accuracy ~0.755-0.760 (>=0.753), time ~8-9 s, complete True. All three trial times within ~3% of each other, since warmup moves into build. If accuracy comes in at 0.750-0.753, the next step is the same recipe at 9.0 epochs.
description: Replace the no-op baseline in submissions/arena/ with the futurebiohackers airbench96-style recipe as published (A1a): frozen 2x2 patch-whitening stem, 3-conv groups at widths 128/384/576, SGD-Nesterov lr 9 with BN biases at 64x LR, label smoothing 0.3, lookahead-EMA, alternating flip + translate 2, 8.5 epochs, bs 1024, fp16 + channels_last, GPU-resident uint8 data with GPU-side augmentation. In build, run torch.compile max-autotune and warm it up on synthetic inputs for both train and eval shapes, including eval batch sizes 1..1024 or dynamic, and the cuDNN/CUDA init. E000 showed lazy init landing in the first timed trial. Log the per-trial prepare and train split.

expected: Mean accuracy within 0.15 pp of A1a, mean time within 2%, per-seed std <=0.35 pp. This sets the threshold below which later time gains count as noise.
description: Rerun the A1a reproduction byte-identical, with no code change, to measure run-to-run time and accuracy noise. Record the per-seed accuracy std and the per-trial prepare/train times from both runs.

expected: Accuracy stays >=0.753 (roughly -0.1 to -0.3 pp vs A1a). Time drops ~10-12%, to about 7.5-8 s.
description: On top of A1a, apply dirac (identity) init to the second and third conv of each group, the parts that map channels to themselves, as in airbench. Cut epochs from 8.5 to 7.5 and change nothing else.
note: Premise false: the reference recipe (E001) already applies dirac init in Conv.reset_parameters to every 3x3 conv (w[:w.size(1)]), so H1.2's 'missing dirac' cannot be tested; the epoch cut alone is covered by I006/epoch sweeps.

expected: Time -2 to -4%, accuracy within ±0.2 pp of A1a.
description: On top of A1a, replace every GELU activation with SiLU (same compile and epochs). If the reference already uses ReLU or SiLU, test GELU->ReLU on whichever activation it does use.

expected: Prepare time -30% or more. If prepare is >=3% of the total, total time falls ~1-2%. Accuracy within ±0.2 pp.
description: On top of A1a, compute the patch-whitening eigendecomposition on the first 1500 training images instead of 5000, and do normalization in fp16 on the GPU in one fused pass. Instrument prepare time separately.

expected: Per-epoch cost +~6-8%, epochs -12%, net time -3 to -5%. Accuracy ~0.754-0.758 (>=0.753).
description: On top of A1a, widen the last group from 576 to 768 channels and cut epochs from 8.5 to 7.5. Recompile and warm up the new shapes in build.

expected: Time -5 to -10% vs A1a. Accuracy -0.1 to -0.4 pp (risk of dropping below 0.753, explore).
description: On top of A1a, train at 24 px for the first ~40% of epochs, 28 px for the next ~30% and 32 px for the rest, with random-resized crops on the GPU. Add +0.5 epochs (9.0 total). Compile and warm up all three shapes in build so no recompile happens in timed code. The final EMA/eval runs at 32 px.

expected: Time -3 to -6% from fewer steps and better utilization. Accuracy -0.2 to -0.6 pp (likely near or below threshold, explore).
description: On top of A1a, raise the batch size from 1024 to 2000 at equal epochs. Scale lr, wd and EMA/lookahead intervals by the kilostep rule: keep lr*wd per example, and scale the step-based schedule by the step count. Warm up the new shapes in build.

expected: Time about 6.80 s (-5.5 to -6%, since 1 epoch is about 0.85 s). Accuracy about 0.751-0.754 (-0.15 to -0.4 pp vs 0.7549). If it is >=0.753 it becomes the new tip. Either way it measures the local accuracy-per-epoch slope that every later epoch-cut idea depends on, and it is the baseline for the brightness/contrast and label-smoothing ideas.
description: Control run for H1.4.1, and the epoch-slope point for H1. Start from A1a (E001 tip) and change only the epoch count, from 8.5 to 8.0. Scale the LR and lookahead/EMA schedule to the new total step count the same way the recipe already does. Leave everything else byte-identical. Log the per-seed accuracies.

expected: Accuracy +0.1 to +0.3 pp over the 8.0-epoch control, giving about 0.753-0.756 (feasible). Time within +0.5% of the control, about 6.80-6.85 s, because the op is cheap. If accuracy does not beat the control by more than about 0.2 pp (the perturbation-noise level), H1.4.1 is refuted.
description: Take the 8.0-epoch recipe from the control idea and add light brightness/contrast jitter in the existing GPU-side augmentation. Per image, multiply by a contrast factor drawn uniformly from [0.85, 1.15] around the per-image mean, then add a brightness offset drawn uniformly from [-0.1, 0.1] (in normalized units), before the flip/translate step. Apply it to training batches only and keep it a single fused elementwise op. Change nothing else.

expected: Accuracy +0.0 to +0.3 pp over the 8.0-epoch control. Time identical to the control (about 6.80 s). If the gain is >=0.2 pp, also retune at 7.5 epochs. If accuracy falls, ls 0.3 is near-optimal and epoch cuts need another source of accuracy.
description: On the 8.0-epoch recipe, lower label smoothing from 0.3 to 0.2. Change nothing else. This tests whether the reference hyperparameters, which were tuned at 8.5 epochs, leave accuracy on the table at shorter schedules. Shorter training usually wants less regularization.

expected: Time -0.3 to -1.5% (about 7.11-7.20 s), most likely short of the >=2% that H3.1.1 predicts, which would refute it and confirm the energy-bound model. Accuracy within ±0.2 pp, from floating-point reordering only. If time falls by >=2%, the power-cap model is wrong about optimizer memory traffic, and more fusion is worth pursuing.
description: Start from A1a. Make the optimizer fused: torch.optim.SGD(fused=True) if PyTorch 2.4 accepts it for this param-group setup, otherwise foreach=True. Wrap the optimizer step plus the lookahead/EMA update in a single torch.compile'd function and warm it up in build on synthetic gradients. Keep the epochs (8.5) and all hyperparameters unchanged. This also tests the E004 power-cap lesson, which predicts little gain from cutting overhead alone.

expected: Time -2 to -6%: each step costs about 0.93x a full step after epoch 2, and less GPU energy. Accuracy -0.3 to -1.0 pp, likely infeasible at 8.5 epochs. The value of the run is the exchange rate. If accuracy loss per % of time saved beats the epoch-cut rate (about 0.35 pp per 6%), combine it with +0.5 epochs. Otherwise H2.3 is refuted for this data size.
description: Start from A1a (8.5 epochs). From the start of epoch 3, for each batch of 1024: (1) run a no-grad forward through the compiled net in train mode, with BN running-stat updates disabled, and get per-example losses; (2) keep the 614 highest-loss examples (a fixed size, so the shapes stay static); (3) run the normal forward+backward and optimizer step on those 614 only. Compile and warm up the 614-shape train step in build. Keep the LR schedule tied to the step count, which does not change.

expected: Time about 6.3-6.5 s, -10 to -13% vs A1a's 7.22 s. Per-epoch costs from E006: 26 px ~0.56, 28 px ~0.65, 32 px ~0.84 s. Accuracy 0.751-0.757: E006 lost 0.69 pp with only 2 full-res epochs and a degenerate 24 px stage; this has 3.6 full-res epochs. If >=0.753 it becomes the new tip. If 0.749-0.753, follow with 9.5 epochs and the same fractions (about +0.35 s).
description: Start from A1a (E001 tip) and add progressive resizing with a long full-res tail. Total 9.0 epochs (LR/EMA/lookahead schedules rescaled to the step count as the recipe already does). Train at 26 px for steps 0-30%, 28 px for 30-60% and 32 px for the last 40%. Low-res batches are made by applying the existing flip + translate-2 at 32 px, then F.interpolate(mode='bilinear', antialias=True) to 26/28 px. No random-resized crop. The final group pool must still end at 3x3 (26->25->12->6->3, 28->27->13->6->3). In build, compile and warm up all 3 train shapes plus eval at 32 px, so nothing recompiles in timed code. Instrumentation only: log a hash of the first batch's augmentation parameters per trial.

expected: Time about 6.1-6.3 s, +4-6% vs E006's 5.88 s, since the 26 px epochs cost ~0.56 s vs 0.47 s. Accuracy 0.750-0.754, i.e. +0.2 to +0.6 pp over E006's 0.748. A gain of >=0.4 pp supports H2.5 (the loss came from confounds, not low resolution). A gain of <0.2 pp means the short full-res tail is the binding factor and favors the H2.1.2 schedule.
description: Take E006's schedule unchanged: 9.0 epochs, epochs 0-3 low-res, 4-6 at 28 px, 7-8 at 32 px. Make exactly two changes, which together are the H2.5 confound removal: (a) the first phase uses 26 px instead of 24 px, and (b) replace random-resized crop with flip + translate-2 at 32 px followed by an antialiased bilinear downsample to the phase resolution. Warm up all shapes in build.

expected: Time 6.80 s ±1% (unchanged). Accuracy +0.1 to +0.4 pp over the control, giving 0.751-0.754. If >=0.753 it becomes the new tip at about 6.80 s (-5.8%) and the change gets ported to the progressive recipe. A gain under 0.2 pp is within perturbation noise and refutes H6.1.1.
description: On the 8.0-epoch recipe (the E007 control, 0.7502 / 6.80 s), change only the LR schedule's end point: decay linearly to 0 at the last step instead of to 0.07x the peak. Keep warmup, peak LR, the BN-bias multiplier and the lookahead/EMA schedule unchanged. Being zero-cost, the resulting accuracy lever can stack onto any progressive-resizing recipe.

expected: Accuracy and time identical to E006 (0.7480, ~5.88 s). Prediction: the hashes differ across seeds 0-2, and repeating seed 0 reproduces them. Then E006's 0.02 pp per-seed spread was chance and H2.1.3 is supported. If the hashes are identical across seeds, or the generator is built in build/import, the progressive line needs a seeding fix and its accuracy numbers need re-measuring.
description: RNG audit for progressive resizing, with no recipe change. Rerun E006's code (commit ed8dc49) adding only logging: per trial, log a hash of the first train batch's augmentation parameters (crop boxes/scales, flip mask, translate offsets) and a hash of the initial model parameters after prepare. Also run seed 0 twice through a side script that calls build/prepare/train in-process. Check the result: augmentation generators must be derived from the trial seed and reset in prepare. If they are not, fix that in every progressive successor. A shared stream would break the no-information-flow and seeding rules.
note: Settled: E013 (same RNG mechanism as E006: all randomness from the global torch RNG that the harness seeds per trial before prepare; no custom generators, none created in build/import) logged different first-batch hashes for seeds 0/1/2 (-5.54e3, -2.25e4, 5.75e3), and E002 showed reruns reproduce per-seed accuracy bit-for-bit. E006's 0.02 pp spread was chance.

expected: Time within ±1% of the H2.1.2 run. Accuracy differs by -0.3 to +0.4 pp. H2.5.2 predicts crop mode wins by >=0.3 pp (FixRes scale argument). If it loses, the network benefits from seeding the full field of view at low res and downsampling is the right operator.
description: Take the H2.1.2 recipe (9.0 epochs; 26 px for 0-30%, 28 px for 30-60%, 32 px for the last 40%). Change only how low-res batches are made. Crop mode: after flip + translate-2 at 32 px, take a random 26x26 or 28x28 crop (independent offset per image, done via unfold/gather or a batched index on the GPU), with no rescaling, so object scale matches the test images. Do not use the antialiased downsample. Keep the shapes identical so the compiled graphs are reused.

expected: Time about 6.4-6.7 s (-8 to -12%). Accuracy 0.746-0.752 (-0.3 to -0.8 pp). If the loss per 1% of time saved is <0.06 pp, it beats epoch cuts and is worth combining with +0.5 epochs or with progressive resizing. Otherwise H2.6 is refuted (capacity is not cheap to remove on CIFAR-100).
description: On A1a (8.5 epochs, everything else unchanged), narrow group 2 from 384 to 320 channels, which also shrinks group 3's first conv input. Recompile and warm up in build. Group 2 at 15x15 carries ~50% of conv FLOPs by a rough count. 384->320 cuts total conv FLOPs by about 15%. The exchange rate to beat is the epoch-cut rate, 0.08 pp per 1% of time (E007).

expected: Time +0.5 to +1.5% (about 5.92-5.97 s). Accuracy +0.0 to +0.3 pp over E006's 0.748. A small gain is likely because E006 already ended with 2 epochs at 32 px. A gain of >=0.2 pp supports H6.2.1 and makes it a cheap add-on for any schedule with a short full-res tail.
description: On E006's code (commit ed8dc49), add only a FixRes-style BN re-estimation at the end of train. After the final EMA/lookahead weights are set, reset the BN running stats and run a forward-only pass in train mode (momentum=None, cumulative average) at 32 px over ~5000 augmented training images (5 batches of 1024, flip + translate only), under no_grad. Warm up this shape in build (it is the existing 32 px train shape).

expected: Time +1 to +4% (7.3-7.5 s), from NS matmuls on small matrices. Accuracy 0.750-0.757. H5.1.1 predicts no gain over SGD of more than 0.2 pp. A gain of >=0.4 pp would refute H5 and justify a Muon run at 8.0 epochs or on the progressive recipe.
description: On A1a (8.5 epochs), switch the 3x3 conv filters of the three groups to Muon: lr ~0.24, momentum 0.6, Nesterov, 3 Newton-Schulz steps in bf16, filters reshaped to [out, in*9]. Keep SGD-Nesterov with the existing hyperparameters for BN params, biases and the head. Keep the LR schedule shape and the lookahead/EMA. Warm up the compiled NS step in build. This is an explore run on the one optimization-efficiency lever not yet tried; E008 suggests the short schedule is under-fitting.

expected: Time about 6.55-6.70 s (8.04 x 7/8.5 = 6.62 s; the Muon per-step overhead scales with steps), i.e. -8 to -9% vs A1a's 7.22 s. Accuracy 0.752-0.760 (0.7663 minus ~1.5 epochs at a 0.5-1.0 pp/epoch slope). If >=0.756 it is a new tip with margin, and H5 is refuted on time-to-75 as well. If 0.750-0.756, the next step is 7.5 epochs or the cheaper Muon step (I023). Below 0.750 means Muon's slope is steeper than SGD's at short schedules.
description: Start from the E019 Muon recipe (commit 45b511c): Muon on the 9 group 3x3 convs, lr 0.24, momentum 0.6, Nesterov, 3 NS steps in bf16; SGD for BN/biases/head; lookahead-EMA. Change only the epoch count, from 8.5 to 7.0. Rescale the LR, lookahead and EMA schedules to the new total step count, the same way the recipe already does (as in E007). Leave the Muon step code eager and unchanged so the run measures the Muon accuracy-vs-epochs slope with no confound. Log per-seed accuracies.

expected: Time 6.2-6.5 s: 4x0.485 + 4x0.848 + ~0.2 overhead = 5.53 s for the SGD part, plus ~0.78 s of eager Muon overhead over ~392 steps. That is -10 to -14% vs A1a. Accuracy 0.754-0.761: an SGD estimate of ~0.746-0.749 for this schedule (between E006 and E007), plus ~1.1 pp from Muon. If >=0.756 it becomes the tip and is the base for the compiled-Muon stack. If Muon's gain shrinks to <0.5 pp under low-res epochs, Muon and progressive resizing overlap (both buy early-phase efficiency).
description: Port the two-stage 24->32 px progressive schedule to the E019 Muon recipe. 8.0 total epochs: epochs 0-3 at 24 px, epochs 4-7 at 32 px, no 28 px phase. Use the E006 operator: flip + translate-2 at 32 px, then F.interpolate(bilinear, antialias=True) to 24 px, with AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) as the final pool. Rescale the LR/EMA/lookahead schedules to the step count. Keep the Muon step eager as in E019. In build, compile and warm up both train shapes and the 32 px eval, so nothing recompiles in timed code.

expected: Time 7.55-7.70 s (E019's 8.04 s minus half of the ~0.82 s Muon overhead; the conv work is unchanged per E010). Accuracy 0.756-0.766: a smaller penalty than SGD's -0.8 pp if Muon tolerates large batches. A loss of <=0.3 pp makes bs 2000 the preferred Muon batch, since it halves the optimizer overhead. A loss of >=0.7 pp confirms that updates per epoch are binding (H1.6) for both optimizers.
description: On E019's Muon recipe at 8.5 epochs, raise the batch size from 1024 to 2000. Scale the SGD param groups (BN/bias/head) by the same kilostep rule as E010, and scale the EMA/lookahead schedule by the step count. Keep Muon lr 0.24 and momentum 0.6, which are airbench94_muon's own settings at bs 2000. Warm up the new shapes in build. This tests whether Muon removes the large-batch penalty SGD showed (E010: -0.81 pp) while halving the per-step Muon overhead.

expected: Time -0.8 to -1.5% vs E019 (about 7.93-7.98 s), because the fused BN+act kernels use less energy (E003: SiLU saved 2.2%). Accuracy within 0.25 pp of 0.7663. If time falls by <0.5%, the erf cost is not the energy driver and elementwise micro-tuning is done.
description: On E019's Muon recipe (8.5 epochs), replace every exact GELU with nn.GELU(approximate='tanh'). Change nothing else, and recompile/warm up in build. Running this on the Muon base means the expected ~1% saving can be kept even with perturbation noise, since that base has 1.3 pp of margin.

expected: Time unchanged vs its base (±0.5%). Accuracy -0.3 to +0.5 pp vs its base. A gain of >=0.3 pp buys ~0.3-0.5 epochs (~4-6% of time) at no cost. A loss means 0.6 is near-optimal, so the next lever is lr, not momentum.
description: Explore Muon hyperparameters, which came untuned from CIFAR-10 airbench94 (bs 2000). On the I022 recipe (Muon, 7.0 epochs), change only the Muon momentum from 0.6 to 0.85 (Nesterov kept, lr 0.24 unchanged). Higher momentum is the usual Muon setting at smaller batches, and bs 1024 gives each step half the gradient averaging of bs 2000. If I022 has not run yet, run this at 8.5 epochs against E019 instead.
note: ideate: Its base is out of date: it targets the I022/E020 recipe, which E021 has superseded. It is re-proposed as Muon momentum 0.85 on the E021 tip.

expected: Time about 5.85-6.05 s, which is -0.3 to -0.45 s (-5 to -7%) vs 6.331 s. The basis is the micro-benchmark: eager Muon adds ~1.9 ms/step, launch-bound with the GPU idle; compiled Muon adds ~0.8 ms/step; the run has ~392 steps. Accuracy 0.754-0.761, changed only by numerics (perturbation noise ~0.25 pp on the mean). If it holds >=0.753, it is the new tip and the base for every later cut. If time falls by <2%, the Muon overhead is energy-bound rather than launch-bound, and bs 2000 (E022) becomes the overhead lever.
description: Start from the E021 tip (commit bf93586: Muon + 4@24 + 4@32 px, 8.0 epochs). Change only how the Muon update runs. Wrap the whole update in a single function: momentum/Nesterov, bf16 3-step Newton-Schulz batched over same-shape filters (conv2/conv3 of each group stacked into one bmm), scale, and the weight update. Compile it with torch.compile(mode='max-autotune-no-cudagraphs'), and pass the LR as a 0-d GPU tensor so the schedule never recompiles. Warm it up in build on synthetic gradients for every filter shape. Keep the math, hyperparameters, schedule and data pipeline unchanged. Log per-trial train time.

expected: Time about 5.95-6.05 s: one epoch moves from 0.848 to 0.485 s, so -0.36 s (-5.7%). Accuracy 0.753-0.757 (-0.1 to -0.5 pp vs 0.7578). H2.7 predicts a loss of <=0.3 pp, i.e. a 24 px epoch keeps most of a 32 px epoch's value, which gives an exchange rate of <=0.05 pp per 1%. A loss of >=0.5 pp means the 32 px share is binding with Muon, and cuts should come from total epochs instead.
description: On the E021 tip, change only the resolution split: 5 epochs at 24 px + 3 epochs at 32 px (was 4 + 4), still 8.0 total. Keep the E006 operator (flip + translate-2 at 32 px, antialiased bilinear downsample), AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1), eager Muon, and LR/EMA/lookahead rescaled to the step count, which does not change. The compiled shapes are already warmed up in build.

expected: 16 px epoch cost <=0.35x a 32 px epoch (~0.25-0.30 s), giving time about 5.85-6.0 s (-5 to -8% vs 6.331). Accuracy 0.752-0.758 (-0.0 to -0.6 pp). If the loss is <=0.3 pp, the very-low-res phase is the cheapest epoch source, and the next step reinvests the savings in +1 epoch. If the 16 px cost is >0.4x (small maps underuse the GPU) or the loss is >=0.5 pp, H2.8 is refuted.
description: Explore sub-24 px phases on the E021 tip. Change only the schedule: 2 epochs at 16 px + 2 at 24 px + 4 at 32 px (8.0 total; the first two 24 px epochs become 16 px). Make the 16 px batches with the same operator (flip + translate-2 at 32 px, then antialiased bilinear to 16 px). The maps become 15/7/3/1, and AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) handles that. Compile and warm up the 16 px train shape in build. Before the scored run, measure the compiled 16 px and 20 px epoch costs with an untimed side script (2 epochs each) and log them next to the existing cost table.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Accuracy -0.3 to +0.5 pp vs 0.7578. A gain of >=0.3 pp is worth ~0.5 Muon-epochs (~5% of time) at zero cost and should then stack with the compiled-Muon tip. A loss means momentum 0.6 is near-optimal, and lr is the next Muon knob to tune.
description: Rebased I026. On the E021 tip, change only the Muon momentum from 0.6 to 0.85 (Nesterov kept, lr 0.24 unchanged). The 0.6/0.24 values come from CIFAR-10 airbench94 at bs 2000. At bs 1024 each step averages half as many examples, which usually favors higher momentum. Leave the SGD groups, schedule and resolution split unchanged.

expected: Time -0.5 to -1.5% (about 6.24-6.30 s), because the fused BN+activation kernels use less energy (E003: SiLU saved 2.2%). Accuracy within ±0.25 pp of 0.7578. If time falls by <0.5%, the erf is not an energy driver and elementwise micro-tuning is closed.
description: Rebased I025. On the E021 tip, replace every exact GELU with nn.GELU(approximate='tanh'). Change nothing else, and recompile/warm up both train shapes and eval in build.
note: Settled by E023: tanh-approximate GELU gave identical accuracy (0.7663 vs 0.7663) but +5.1% time on the Muon base; under Inductor the tanh form is more arithmetic than exact erf, so it cannot save time on the tip either.

expected: Mean over seeds 3-10 is 0.754-0.759, std ~0.3-0.4 pp, so the tip clears the official 75% with ~0.4+ pp to spare, and future cut rounds may spend down to ~0.755 on seeds 0-2. If the mean is <0.752, seeds 0-2 are a favorable draw, and future tips need a 3-seed mean >=0.757.
description: Margin check on the current tip, with no recipe change. Using an untimed side script, run the E021 submission through the benchmark's own trial code (import it, do not edit benchmark/) on extra seeds 3-10, and record per-seed accuracy and time. The scored run is unchanged (just repeat E021) so the loop has a row, or skip scoring if the harness allows. This gauges whether the 3-seed 0.7578 reflects the 40-seed mean before margin is spent on cuts (the tip's seed 2 was 0.7523).

expected: The 32 px phase sits at the cap for >=80% of its time. The 24 px phase sits below 90% of the cap for >=30% of its time, because its small maps plus eager Muon launches leave GPU gaps. That would predict compiled Muon saves proportionally more in the 24 px phase, and that overhead fixes (H3-style) matter again under low-res training. Accuracy and time identical to E021 (±0.5%).
description: Observational, on the E021 tip with no recipe change. During one scored run, sample board power and SM clock via NVML at >=10 Hz in a separate monitoring process launched outside the submission (no sleeps inside submission code). Tag the samples by phase using logged CUDA-event timestamps for the 24 px phase, the 32 px phase and the eager Muon steps. Report the fraction of time at >=95% of the 400 W cap for each phase.
note: ideate: Stale base: it assumes eager Muon on E021. Compiled Muon (E024) and the 16 px phase (E026) change what each phase is bound by. Re-proposed as per-phase power sampling on the E026 tip.

expected: Time about 5.28-5.35 s, -3 to -4% vs 5.501 s: one epoch drops from ~0.485 s to ~0.27 s. Accuracy 0.753-0.757, i.e. -0.0 to -0.3 pp; E026 cost ~0.15 pp per 24->16 epoch swap. If it is >=0.753, it is the new tip and shows the early phase tolerates 16 px across 3/8 of training. A loss of >=0.4 pp means the 24 px bridge epoch is what carries the transfer to 32 px, and the next cut should look elsewhere.
description: On the E026 tip (commit da18628: compiled batched Muon, 2@16 + 2@24 + 4@32 px, 8.0 epochs), change only the schedule to 3@16 + 1@24 + 4@32 px, so epoch 2 moves from 24 px to 16 px. Keep the same operator (flip + translate-2 at 32 px, then antialiased bilinear downsample), AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1), and Muon/SGD hyperparameters. The step count is unchanged, so the LR/EMA/lookahead schedules are unchanged too. All shapes are already warmed up in build.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%, ~5.50 s). Accuracy -0.3 to +0.4 pp vs 0.7565. A gain of >=0.3 pp buys ~0.5 epoch-equivalents at zero cost and becomes the tip (more margin for schedule cuts). A loss of >=0.3 pp brackets 0.6 as near-optimal, and momentum tuning is closed.
description: On the E026 tip, change only the Muon momentum from 0.6 to 0.5 (Nesterov kept, lr 0.24, compiled update unchanged; pass momentum so nothing recompiles, or rewarm in build). E027 showed 0.85 costs 1.18 pp. This tests the other direction, since the lookahead-EMA and Nesterov already smooth the iterates and the 0.6 value was tuned on CIFAR-10 at bs 2000 without lookahead.

expected: Time -1.5 to -3% (about 5.35-5.42 s). Accuracy -0.3 to +0.1 pp (a less orthogonalized update). If accuracy holds >=0.753 with time -1.5% or better, it is the new tip. If time falls by <1%, the residual Muon cost is in momentum/cast/update traffic rather than NS, and the remaining lever is bs 2000 for Muon.
description: On the E026 tip, change only the number of Newton-Schulz iterations in the compiled batched Muon update, from 3 to 2 (same quintic coefficients, bf16). Re-warm the compiled update in build for every filter shape. Everything else is identical. The remaining Muon overhead is ~1 ms/step x 384 steps (~0.4 s, ~7% of the run), and the NS matmuls are most of it; per the E019 micro-benchmark, eager GPU time fell 3.8 -> 2.8 ms with 2 steps.

expected: Accuracy and time of the scored run identical to E026 (0.7565, ~5.50 s). Mean over seeds 3-10 is 0.752-0.757, std ~0.3-0.4 pp. If it is >=0.754, later cut rounds may spend down to ~0.753 on seeds 0-2. If it is <0.752, seeds 0-2 are a favourable draw, and future tips need a 3-seed mean >=0.756.
description: Margin check on the current tip (E026, replacing the stale I032, which targeted E021), with no recipe change. In an untimed side script, import the arena submission and run it through the benchmark's own trial code (do not edit benchmark/) on extra seeds 3-10. Record per-seed accuracy and time. For the scored row, repeat E026 unchanged. This calibrates how much of the 0.35 pp margin on seeds 0-2 is real before more is spent on cuts.
note: Done as I032/E028 on the E026 tip: seeds 3-10 via the harness gave mean 0.75528 (sd 0.22 pp), and the scored rerun of the tip gave 0.7543 (non-deterministic vs E026's 0.7565); tip true accuracy ~0.7554.

expected: Time about 5.05-5.15 s (-6.5 to -8% vs 5.501 s). Accuracy 0.749-0.755 (-0.1 to -0.7 pp). If it is >=0.753, it is the new tip at the best exchange rate yet. If the loss is >=0.5 pp while 3@16 + 1@24 holds, the last pre-tail epoch needs >=24 px.
description: Explore the limit of the very-low-res early phase. On the E026 tip, change only the schedule to 4@16 + 4@32 px (8.0 epochs, no 24 px phase). Same operator, same Muon/SGD hyperparameters, same step count and schedules. 16 px and 32 px shapes are already warmed up in build. This is the aggressive end of the line, beyond the 3@16 + 1@24 variant, and tests whether a 24 px bridge is needed at all.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Accuracy -0.4 to +0.4 pp vs 0.7565. A gain of >=0.3 pp gives free margin to spend on the schedule cuts. A loss of >=0.3 pp suggests 0.24 is at or below the optimum, so a follow-up at 0.30 is warranted.
description: On the E026 tip, change only the Muon learning rate from 0.24 to 0.18 (the shape of the schedule is unchanged; the LR is passed as the existing 0-d GPU tensor, so nothing recompiles). E027 suggested that larger effective Muon steps overshoot in this short, lookahead-averaged schedule. This tests whether a smaller step size helps at bs 1024 (0.24 was tuned at bs 2000 on CIFAR-10).
note: H5 refuted

expected: Accuracy and time identical to E026 (±0.5%). The 32 px phase sits at the cap for >=80% of its time. The 16 px phase sits below 90% of the cap for >=30% of its time (small maps, per-step Muon and launch costs dominate). If so, the early phase is overhead-bound, and per-step fixes (bs 2000 in the 16 px phase only, fewer NS steps) pay off there specifically.
description: Observational, on the E026 tip with no recipe change (replacing the stale I033, which assumed eager Muon on E021). During one scored run, sample board power and SM clock via NVML at >=10 Hz in a separate monitoring process launched outside the submission (no sleeps in submission code). Tag samples by phase (16 px, 24 px, 32 px) using logged CUDA-event timestamps. Report, per phase, the fraction of time at >=95% of the 400 W cap and the mean SM clock.

expected: Time +2 to +2.6% (about 5.62-5.65 s; one NS iteration measured at ~0.124 s per trial in E031). Accuracy 0.756-0.760, i.e. +0.1 to +0.5 pp over the 0.7554 tip estimate. If the gain is >=0.3 pp (3-seed mean >=0.7585), this beats every epoch exchange rate (0.035-0.08 pp per 1%). The next step then stacks it on the 3@16 + 1@24 + 4@32 near-miss (E029: -0.27 s for -0.31 pp), for about 5.36 s at ~0.755. If the gain is <0.15 pp, 3 iterations are already saturated, and NS work is closed in both directions.
description: On the E026 tip (commit da18628: compiled batched Muon, 2@16 + 2@24 + 4@32 px, 8.0 epochs), change only the Newton-Schulz iteration count in the compiled Muon update from 3 to 4. Keep the quintic coefficients (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315), bf16, batching and everything else. Re-warm the compiled update in build for every filter shape. E031 showed the opposite direction (3 -> 2) costs 1.82 pp for -2.3% time. So orthogonalization quality is an accuracy knob, and one more iteration may buy margin at ~0.32 ms/step. Log per-seed accuracy and per-trial train time.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%, ~5.50 s). Accuracy +0.0 to +0.5 pp over the 0.7554 estimate, because the orthogonalization is better at equal cost (E031: quality matters by ~1.8 pp per iteration). A 3-seed mean >=0.7575 makes it the new tip with free margin to spend on a 3rd 16 px epoch. A result at or below 0.7554 means the fixed coefficients are already good enough at 3 steps, and only the iteration count (the NS-4 idea) remains.
description: On the E026 tip, keep 3 Newton-Schulz iterations but replace the fixed quintic coefficients with per-iteration optimal coefficients for a 3-step schedule. Compute them offline with the Polar Express procedure (arXiv 2505.16932): minimax-optimal odd quintics for the singular-value interval [l, 1] with l about 1e-3, and a small safety factor (~1.01) for bf16. Hard-code them as constants. Before the scored run, do an untimed check that the singular values of a random 384x3456 bf16 matrix land closer to 1 (report min/max) than with the fixed coefficients. Same FLOPs, so time should be unchanged. Re-warm the compiled update in build.
note: Settled by E033 + spectrum analysis (E033 Outcome): on the real Muon-input spectra, fixed-quintic x4 already puts 83% of singular values in [0.7,1.3] (x3: 56%) and gave no accuracy gain (E033); 3-step Polar-Express coefficients with l=1e-3 are worse than fixed x3 (21%), and with l=1e-2 they only match x4 (83%). Same FLOPs, so no time gain is possible either.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Accuracy -0.2 to +0.4 pp vs 0.7554. H7.1.2 is supported at >=0.7575. A result of <=0.7535 suggests 0.24 is at or below the optimum, so a probe at 0.28 is warranted. Anything in between is noise, and the Muon hyperparameters are closed.
description: On the E026 tip, change only the Muon learning rate from 0.24 to 0.20 (momentum 0.6, Nesterov, same schedule shape; the LR is already a 0-d GPU tensor, so nothing recompiles). Both independently tuned public Muon recipes use 0.205-0.2255. E030 showed momentum is flat between 0.5 and 0.6, so lr is the one Muon knob left untested (the dropped I039 never ran).

expected: Time -0.5 to -2% (about 5.39-5.47 s). Renorm is a norm plus a scale over 9 filters, probably ~0.05-0.15 ms/step, so the >=1.5% that H7.2.1 predicts is optimistic. Accuracy within ±0.25 pp of 0.7554. If time falls by <0.7%, renorm is not a meaningful part of the Muon overhead, and what remains is NS matmuls plus momentum traffic, which only batch size can cut.
description: On the E026 tip, change only how often the Muon-managed conv filters are renormalized: every 2 + int(15*progress) steps instead of every step (hiverge/Fable style). Do it inside the compiled update with a 0-d bool/int tensor flag (torch.where-gated, or two warmed-up variants selected on the host) so nothing recompiles in timed code. Warm up both paths in build. Everything else is unchanged. Before scoring, log per-step update time with CUDA events in an untimed run, to separate the renorm cost from NS.

expected: Time +0 to +1.5% (5.50-5.58 s). Accuracy within noise of 0.7554. If the seed-0 repeat is bit-identical, run-to-run noise is gone. Seed-paired comparisons then become possible, which roughly halves the noise on recipe differences (~0.2 pp sd now). The setting should become the default whenever its cost is <=0.5%. If the repeat still differs, the non-determinism comes from the net's own max-autotune picks for the new 16/24 px shapes or from atomics in the backward pass, and H4.3 is refuted.
description: Determinism probe on the E026 tip, with no change to the math or hyperparameters. Compile the Muon update with mode='default' instead of 'max-autotune-no-cudagraphs', and set torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=False with cudnn.deterministic=True for all train/eval shapes. Keep the net's own compile as is. Warm everything up in build. Run the scored evaluation, then rerun seed 0 once in an untimed side script through the benchmark's trial code and compare per-seed accuracy bit for bit.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Accuracy -0.3 to +0.4 pp vs 0.7554. H6.3.1 is supported at >=0.7575, which would give free slack for the E029 3@16 schedule. A result of <=0.7535 confirms LS 0.3 is optimal under Muon too, and zero-cost loss tuning is closed for good.
description: On the E026 tip, change only label smoothing from 0.3 to 0.2. Change nothing else. LS 0.3 was tuned under SGD (E009). Muon fits faster, and tuned public Muon recipes use much lower LS (0.09), so the Muon tip may be over-regularized.

expected: Time -2 to -3.5% (about 5.31-5.39 s): ~128 fewer steps x ~1 ms of Muon, plus per-step SGD/launch costs in the small-map phases. Accuracy -0.05 to -0.35 pp (0.752-0.755). If accuracy is >=0.753 with time <=5.40 s, it is the new tip. A loss of >=0.4 pp means Muon's batch tolerance shrinks at short schedules, so per-step overhead should be attacked inside the update instead.
description: On the E026 tip, raise the batch size from 1024 to 1536 (2@16 + 2@24 + 4@32 px, still 8.0 epochs). Scale the SGD param groups (BN/bias/head) by the E010 kilostep rule. Keep Muon lr 0.24 and momentum 0.6. Rescale the LR warmup/decay, EMA and lookahead schedules to the new step count (~256 steps). Compile and warm up the 1536-batch shapes at 16/24/32 px in build. The remaining Muon cost is per step (~1 ms), so a third fewer steps cuts it directly. E022 showed Muon tolerates large batches (-0.25 pp at bs 2000).

expected: Time about 5.19-5.24 s (-4.5 to -5% vs 5.472 s, as in E029). Accuracy 0.752-0.756: the E035 family estimate of ~0.756-0.757 minus ~0.3 pp. New tip only under the H4 rule (3-seed mean >=0.755, or >=0.753 now plus a confirming rerun that averages >=0.7535). Below 0.752 means E035's +0.18 pp was noise and the third 16 px epoch stays unaffordable.
description: On the E035 tip (compiled batched Muon with renorm every 2+int(15*progress) steps, 2@16 + 2@24 + 4@32 px, 8.0 epochs), change only the schedule to 3@16 + 1@24 + 4@32 px, so epoch 2 moves from 24 px to 16 px. This is E029's schedule moved onto the newer base. Use the same operator (flip + translate-2 at 32 px, then antialiased bilinear downsample) and AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1). The step count is unchanged, so the LR/EMA/lookahead/renorm schedules are unchanged. All shapes are already warmed up in build. This combines two near-misses: E029 (-0.27 s for -0.31 pp, infeasible by 0.0007) and E035's possible +0.18 pp. It does not rerun E029 unchanged (H4.2).

expected: Time about 5.24-5.32 s (-2.8 to -4.2%): 2 epochs x (0.485 - ~0.36 s). Accuracy -0.05 to -0.3 pp vs the tip family, i.e. 0.754-0.757. If the loss is <=0.2 pp, this beats E029's exchange rate (<=0.05 pp per 1%) and becomes the tip. It would also suggest that the bridge needs a 2x2 final map, not 24 px specifically. A loss of >=0.35 pp means the bridge value comes from resolution, so keep 24 px.
description: On the E035 tip, change only the two 24 px epochs (epochs 2-3) to 20 px: 2@16 + 2@20 + 4@32, 8.0 epochs. Use the same operator (flip + translate-2 at 32 px, antialiased bilinear to 20 px). The maps become 19/9/4/2, and AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) handles that. Compile and warm up the 20 px train shape in build. Step count and schedules are unchanged. This is an intermediate point between the 24 px bridge, which E032 showed matters (-0.68 pp without it), and a third 16 px epoch (E029, -0.31 pp). The goal is a bridge that costs ~0.40-0.45x instead of 0.57x. Log the compiled per-epoch cost of the 20 px phase.

expected: Time +0 to +1% vs 5.472 s, since E019's micro-benchmark gap between default and max-autotune for the Muon update is small next to E036's +9.8%, which came from cuDNN. Accuracy within noise of ~0.756. If all three seed-0 runs are bit-identical, the non-determinism came from the Muon autotune picks. This mode then becomes the default, and later comparisons can be seed-paired (roughly halving decision noise). If they differ, cuDNN benchmark picks per process are the source, and determinism costs ~10%, so it is not worth it.
description: Determinism ablation on the E035 tip, isolating half (a) of E036. Compile the Muon update with mode='default' instead of 'max-autotune-no-cudagraphs'. Keep torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=True and do NOT set cudnn.deterministic, so the net's convs keep their benchmarked algorithms. Warm everything up in build. Run the scored evaluation. Then, in an untimed side script, rerun seed 0 twice in fresh processes through the benchmark's trial code and compare per-seed accuracy bit for bit against the scored seed 0.

expected: Time -1.5 to -3% (about 5.31-5.39 s): ~96 fewer steps x (~1 ms Muon + per-step SGD/launch), more if the small-map phases are launch-bound. Accuracy -0.0 to -0.25 pp, since the early phase is tolerant and the 32 px tail is untouched. If it is >=0.753 with time <=5.40 s, it is the new tip and stacks with any schedule change. A time gain of <1% means the low-res phases are not per-step-bound (consistent with I040 finding them at the power cap).
description: On the E035 tip, use bs 2048 for the low-res phases only (the 2 epochs at 16 px and the 2 at 24 px) and keep bs 1024 for the 4@32 px tail. The goal is to halve the number of fixed-cost Muon/launch steps exactly where they are the largest share of epoch time: 16 px epochs are ~0.27 s with ~49 steps at ~1 ms of Muon each. Drive the LR/EMA/lookahead/renorm schedules by samples seen (progress = examples/total), not by step index. For the bs 2048 steps, scale the SGD groups (BN/bias/head) by the E010 kilostep rule and keep Muon lr 0.24 and momentum 0.6 (E022: Muon tolerates bs 2000). Compile and warm up the 2048-batch 16/24 px shapes in build. Run this independently of the global bs 1536 idea, since it targets the phase-local overhead.

expected: Time +0.3 to +1% (one more small NS matmul per step). Accuracy -0.4 to +0.4 pp vs the ~0.756 tip family. If the gain is >=0.25 pp (3-seed >=0.7585), it gives slack to spend on a 3rd 16 px epoch or a 20 px bridge. A loss means the head wants SGD's unnormalized, scale-sensitive updates (consistent with airbench), and the optimizer-assignment line is closed.
description: Explore a new accuracy source. On the E035 tip, move the classifier head (the linear 576->100 after the global max pool) from SGD to the compiled Muon update. Treat its weight as a [100, 576] matrix and use Muon lr scaled by sqrt(max(1, out/in)) as for the filters, with the same momentum and 3 NS steps. Leave the head's renorm/scale handling as in the SGD version and keep the bias on SGD. Add the shape to the compiled update and warm it up in build. CIFAR-100's 100-way head is a much larger share of the learning problem than CIFAR-10's 10-way head, and public Muon recipes tuned on CIFAR-10 never tried it.

expected: 12 px epoch cost about 0.22-0.26x of a 32 px epoch (floor from Muon's fixed per-step cost and small kernels), so time is only -0.05 to -0.09 s (-1 to -1.6%), about 5.38-5.42 s. Accuracy -0.0 to -0.25 pp. If the cost is >=0.22x and the saving is <1.5%, H2.8.2 is supported and sub-16 px is closed. A 12 px cost of <=0.18x with a loss of <=0.1 pp would reopen very-low-res early phases.
description: On the E035 tip, change only epoch 0 from 16 px to 12 px: 1@12 + 1@16 + 2@24 + 4@32 px, 8.0 epochs. Use the same operator (antialiased bilinear to 12 px). The maps become 11/5/2/1, and AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) handles that. Compile and warm up the 12 px shape in build. Before the scored run, measure the compiled 12 px epoch cost (2 epochs, untimed side script) and log it in the cost table next to 16 px (0.32x).
note: ideate: The base is out of date: it targets the E035 tip at bs 1024, and E038/E044 have superseded it. The best case it predicts is a saving under 1.6%. E041 (20 px) and E040 (a third 16 px epoch) show that further resolution cuts cost more accuracy per second than expected. The new margin is better spent on the 3@16 swap or the fractional trim, and the per-phase profiling idea will measure the floor of the small-map cost anyway.

expected: Time about 4.98-5.03 s (-4 to -5% vs 5.237 s): one 24 px epoch (~0.50 s at bs 1536) becomes a 16 px epoch (~0.27 s). Accuracy 0.7525-0.7550: E044's 0.7574 minus the 0.3-0.5 pp that the third 16 px swap cost in E029/E040. If the 3-seed mean is >=0.755, or >=0.753 with a confirming rerun averaging >=0.7535, it is the new tip. Below 0.752 means the head-Muon margin is not enough to buy this swap, so try the fractional trim instead.
description: On the E044 tip (bs 1536, compiled batched Muon on the 9 group convs plus the 576->100 head, renorm every 2+int(15*progress) steps, 2@16 + 2@24 + 4@32 px, 8.0 epochs), change only the schedule to 3@16 + 1@24 + 4@32 px, so epoch 2 moves from 24 px to 16 px. This is the E029/E040 near-miss moved onto the base that has margin. Keep the operator the same: flip + translate-2 at 32 px, then antialiased bilinear downsample, with AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1). The step count is unchanged, so LR, EMA, lookahead and renorm are unchanged. The 1536-batch 16 px shape is already warmed up in build. New tip only under the H4 rule.

expected: Time about 4.96-5.01 s (-4.5 to -5.5%): half a 24 px epoch (~0.25 s) plus ~0.02 s of Muon/per-step cost. Accuracy 0.7540-0.7560, i.e. -0.15 to -0.35 pp vs 0.7574 (Muon slope ~0.54 pp/epoch, a 24 px epoch worth ~half a 32 px one). If the loss is <=0.25 pp, the exchange rate is <=0.05 pp per 1% and fractional trimming becomes the fine-tuning knob for the remaining margin. A loss of >=0.4 pp means the 24 px bridge is binding at its current length.
description: On the E044 tip, cut half of the 24 px phase using a step-indexed switch: 2@16 + 1.5@24 + 4@32 px, 7.5 total epochs. Rescale the LR warmup/decay, EMA, lookahead and renorm schedules to the new total step count, the same way the recipe already does for epoch changes. Change nothing else, and use only shapes that are already warmed up. This tests whether a fractional removal of a cheap mid-resolution epoch, which also removes Muon steps, trades better than swapping 24 px for 16 px.

expected: Scored rerun 0.7550-0.7580 at ~5.24 s (±0.5%). Seeds 3-10 mean 0.754-0.758 (sd ~0.2-0.3 pp). If the rerun plus E044 average >=0.7560 and seeds 3-10 average >=0.7545, the margin is real (~0.25-0.3 pp spendable). If the two-run mean is <0.7555, E044 was lucky by ~0.2 pp, so only the smaller of the two schedule cuts is affordable.
description: Margin check on the E044 tip (head on Muon), with no recipe change. For the scored row, rerun E044 unchanged; this is the second variance sample on the current tip. In an untimed side script, import the arena submission and run it through the benchmark's own trial code (do not edit benchmark/) on seeds 3-10. Record per-seed accuracy and time. This calibrates whether E044's +0.32 pp is real before it gets spent on schedule cuts.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%, ~5.24 s). Accuracy -0.3 to +0.4 pp vs 0.7574. If the 3-seed mean is >=0.7595 (+0.2 pp), it is free margin and becomes the tip. If it is <=0.7550, try 2x instead, since the head then wants larger steps. A result within ±0.15 pp closes head LR tuning.
description: On the E044 tip, change only the Muon learning rate of the classifier head group (the [100, 576] weight added in E044) from 0.24x to 0.5x of the filter Muon LR, i.e. 0.12 peak on the same schedule shape. Pass it as a separate 0-d GPU tensor so nothing recompiles. Keep the conv-filter Muon LR, momentum, NS steps and the head bias on SGD unchanged. The head's spectral-norm step size was copied from the conv filters untuned. Output layers usually want smaller normalized updates (muP-style), and the head has no renorm or wd to bound it.

expected: Time -3 to -4.5% (about 5.00-5.08 s); the gain is larger in the 32 px tail and smaller in the per-step-bound 16 px phase. Accuracy -0.15 to -0.35 pp vs 0.7574 (0.754-0.756). A loss of <=0.06 pp per 1% saved supports H2.13 and makes width a third axis to combine with schedule trims. A loss of >=0.4 pp means capacity stays expensive under Muon on CIFAR-100, which closes width cuts.
description: On the E044 tip, narrow group 2 from 384 to 352 channels, which also shrinks group 3's first conv input. Muon handles the new filter shapes (re-batch the same-shape stacks). Recompile and warm up every train/eval shape and the Muon update in build. Change nothing else. This lever cuts FLOPs, so it should transfer to the 300 W PCIe judge better than per-step levers. Under SGD, 384->320 cost 0.115 pp per 1% (E017). Muon halved the epoch slope, so it may now trade at <=0.06 pp per 1%.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Accuracy -0.2 to +0.35 pp vs 0.7574. A 3-seed mean >=0.7595 supports H6.4.1 and gives free slack. If the result is within ±0.15 pp, warmup is closed (skip the doubling run). A result <=0.7545 means the warmup is protecting the high SGD LR on BN biases, so it stays.
description: On the E044 tip, change only the LR warmup length, halving it in steps for both the SGD and Muon groups, with the same peak and the same decay end point. Everything else is unchanged. With bs 1536 the run has only ~256 steps, and the warmup was rescaled from a schedule tuned for ~408 SGD steps. Muon's normalized updates need less warmup than high-LR SGD.

expected: Accuracy/time identical to E044 within noise (~0.755-0.758, ~5.24 s). Prediction: wall exceeds GPU-busy by >=30% at 16 px and >=15% at 24 px, <10% at 32 px. Augmentation+downsample is >=10% of 16 px step time. If gaps are >=30% at 16/24 px, queue CUDA-graphing those shapes. If augmentation is >=10%, queue per-phase pre-downsampling of the uint8 dataset (in train) with flip + translate at low res. If both are small, the low-res phases are compute-bound and per-step levers are closed.
description: Observational, on the E044 tip, with no recipe change in the scored path. In an untimed side script (same build, one trial, seed 0), wrap each phase (16/24/32 px) with CUDA events. Using torch.profiler on ~20 steps per phase, split per-step time into data augmentation (flip + translate at 32 px + antialiased downsample), net fwd/bwd, SGD foreach step, compiled Muon update, lookahead/EMA, and GPU-idle gaps. Report wall time vs GPU-busy time per phase. For the scored row, rerun E044 unchanged; it doubles as a variance sample. This gates CUDA graphs (H2.12.1) and a low-res pre-downsampled data path.

expected: Prepare drops from ~60 ms to <=25 ms. Total time -0.5 to -0.9% (about 5.19-5.21 s). Accuracy within noise of 0.7574 (±0.25 pp). If total time falls by <0.3% even though prepare is faster, the work just moves into train (async GPU), and fixed overhead is closed for good.
description: On the E044 tip, cut only fixed timed overhead in prepare. Vectorize the dirac init over all 3x3 convs, and do the uint8->normalized conversion in one fused fp16 GPU op. Keep the whitening statistics on the same 5000 images, so the learned function is unchanged apart from numerics. Make sure all lazy CUDA/cuBLAS/cuDNN handles used in prepare are already initialized in build. Log the prepare and train split per trial. E004 tried this under the SGD power cap, where hidden CPU work cost nothing. In the current 5.2 s run, prepare's ~60 ms fixed cost is ~1% of time and is not overlapped with GPU-bound training.

expected: Time ~4.87-4.89 s (-1.3 to -1.7% vs 4.955 s; E045's micro-benchmark measured ~0.086 s/trial, mostly in the 24 and 32 px phases). Accuracy unchanged within noise (~0.753-0.756). If it is >=0.7535 with time <=4.89 s, bank it as the new tip; a math-identical change only needs the time improvement plus accuracy inside the noise band. If time drops by <0.5%, the micro-benchmark gain does not survive the full run and H2.14.1 is refuted.
description: On the E046 tip (bs 1536, 3@16 + 1@24 + 4@32 px, compiled Muon on 9 convs plus head), set torch._dynamo.config.automatic_dynamic_shapes=False and raise torch._dynamo.config.cache_size_limit (e.g. 64) so that each (resolution, batch) train shape (16/24/32 px at bs 1536, plus any partial last-batch shapes) compiles as its own static graph. Warm all of them up in build on synthetic data. Keep eval on a separate compiled function that is dynamic in the batch dimension (torch._dynamo.mark_dynamic on dim 0, or the existing eval path unchanged), so any B from 1 to 1024 never recompiles. In an untimed side check, verify eval for B in {1, 7, 1000, 1024} returns finite [B,100] logits in under 5 s with no recompile. Change no math, hyperparameters or schedule. Log per-phase epoch times.

expected: Time -0.12 to -0.14 s (~-2.5%, about 4.75 s if the static-shape tip is banked, or ~4.83 s on E046). Accuracy -0.05 to -0.12 pp, two-run mean ~0.7537-0.7545. New tip only under the H4 rule (3-seed mean >=0.755, or two non-bit-identical runs averaging >=0.7535). A loss of >=0.2 pp means the third 16 px swap already made the 24 px bridge binding, and H2.10's fractional-trim line on the bridge is closed.
description: On the static-shape tip (or on E046 if H2.14.1 fails), trim a quarter of the remaining 24 px bridge with a step-indexed switch: 3@16 + 0.75@24 + 4@32 px (7.75 epochs). Rescale the LR warmup/decay, EMA, lookahead and renorm schedules to the new total step count, exactly as E047 did. Change nothing else, and use only shapes already warmed up in build. This trim is half the size of H2.10.2's arm A on purpose: at ~0.03 pp per 1%, the ~0.15 pp margin only covers a ~2-3% trim, while arm A (-0.26 s) would be expected to land at ~0.7532, right on the gate.

expected: Time -0.3 to -1% (roughly -0.015 to -0.05 s), with most of the gain in the backward pass of the 16 px phase (1x1 final map) and the 24 px phase (2x2 final map). Accuracy within noise (>=0.7535). Bank it if time drops >=0.5% with accuracy in the noise band. A drop under 0.3% is time noise, which closes the pool lever.
description: On the static-shape tip (or on E046 if that fails), replace AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) with x.flatten(2).amax(dim=2), which is mathematically identical (Fable: it avoids slow atomic kernels). Recompile and warm up every train and eval shape in build. Change nothing else.

description: On the E046 tip, train the whitening-stem bias only for the first 20% of steps and freeze it after that (as in hiverge and Fable). Set its LR to 0 from step 0.2*total, either through its own 0-d LR tensor or by masking it in the SGD foreach step, so nothing recompiles. Everything else is unchanged. This tests whether the 64x-LR bias groups add late-phase noise in the ~256-step regime.

A pool of 0.7540 or higher, i.e. +0.09 pp over the family's 0.7531 and a 3-run pool of at least 0.7545 together with E049, passes the H4 rule and makes this the new tip at about 4.67 s. description: Base: E060 code, which is the E057 tip (static shapes, max(dim).values pool, Muon floor 0.05) plus E060's vectorized dirac init and fused fp16 normalization in prepare. Both prepare changes are math-neutral, so the result still belongs to the pooled family, which E060 brings to 8 runs with a mean of 0.7531. Change only the head's Muon learning rate: set it to 0.5x the filter Muon LR (0.12 peak, same schedule shape and floor) as its own 0-d GPU tensor, so nothing recompiles. Leave everything else unchanged. Score it twice. Instrumentation only: log the submission source hash and a per-seed checksum of the final weights and BN buffers (for H4.4.1).

expected: Time 4.60-4.65 s, i.e. -0.5 to -1.5% against E060's 4.675 s and -1.5 to -2.5% against the 4.717 s tip. Most of the gain should come from the energy-bound 32 px tail. Two-run pooled accuracy 0.7522-0.7545, within noise of 0.7531. If the drop against E060 is under 0.3%, the dgrad is not being skipped, or it is negligible, and the FLOP channel of H2.15 is refuted. If accuracy pools at 0.7540 or higher, it also supports H8.1's bias-LR channel.
description: Base: E060 code. After 20% of total steps, which falls inside the 16 px phase, set the whitening-stem bias to requires_grad=False. The stem's weights are already frozen, so the stem then has no trainable parameters, and autograd skips group-1 conv1's input gradient (dgrad) for every later step at 16, 24 and 32 px. Compile separate static train graphs keyed by whether the bias takes a gradient, and warm up every (resolution, flag) shape in build on synthetic data. Remove the bias from the SGD foreach step at the switch, or give it a zero LR with a None grad that is skipped. Change nothing else. Before scoring, check in an untimed run that the compiled backward graph has no stem-side convolution_backward input-grad. Score it twice.
note: Settled by E061 + code: the recipe already detaches the whitening bias after whiten_bias_epochs (forward(x, whiten_bias_grad=False) -> b.detach()), so the stem has no trainable inputs and the compiled backward already skips group-1 conv1's dgrad in those steps. E061 moved that switch from 37.5% to 20% of steps exactly as I070 proposes: -0.3% time (4.701 vs 4.717 s), accuracy 0.7523 (noise).

expected: Time 4.66-4.71 s: E047 matched E046 within 0.2%, so this should be equal to E060 within 0.5%. Two-run pooled accuracy 0.7535-0.7555, i.e. +0.05 to +0.2 pp over 0.7531. A pool of 0.7540 or higher makes it the new tip at about 4.68 s (H4 rule) and leaves room for a later fractional trim. If both runs land at 0.7530 or below, E047's 0.7558 was a lucky draw and the 3@16 swap is as good as the reshuffle.
description: Base: E060 code. Change only the schedule to E047's 2@16 + 1.5@24 + 4@32 px: 7.5 total epochs with step-indexed resolution switches, and LR warmup/decay, the Muon floor, EMA, lookahead and the renorm cadence all rescaled to the new total step count, as E047 did. All three bs-1536 static shapes are already warmed up in build. Score it twice. This is the equal-time reshuffle against the 3@16 + 1@24 swap that the current tip uses.

expected: Time -0.5 to -2% against E060's 4.675 s (about 4.58-4.65 s), with the largest saving in the 24 and 32 px phases, whose elementwise kernels are energy- and memory-bound. Accuracy within noise (0.7520-0.7545). A drop under 0.3% means Inductor's default configs for these kernels are already near-optimal, so the next step is a hand-written fused BN-apply+GELU kernel, and only if H2.16.1 shows at least 4 passes.
description: Base: E060 code. The change is Inductor kernel tuning only, aimed at the fused BN/GELU/elementwise Triton kernels, which take about 30% of GPU time (E052). Set torch._inductor.config.coordinate_descent_tuning=True and torch._inductor.config.max_autotune_pointwise=True (the net already compiles with max-autotune) before compiling the net, then recompile and warm up every static train shape plus the eval path in build. Log build time; it must stay under 600 s, and if tuning would exceed that, drop max_autotune_pointwise first. The math is unchanged apart from reduction order. Smoke-test that the loss stays finite for 10 steps before scoring.

expected: Scored row: about 4.675 s, accuracy 0.752-0.755, which adds one run to the family pool. The profile should show elementwise/reduction kernels at 25-35% of 32 px GPU time and at least 4 activation-sized passes per BN+GELU (forward stats, apply+GELU, backward recompute, backward reduction+apply). If they take under 15% of the time or already run at 2 passes or fewer, H2.16 is refuted and the fused-kernel line is closed.
description: Observational. Run an untimed side script on the E060 code with the same build and one trial on seed 0. Use torch.profiler for about 20 steps of the 32 px phase at bs 1536, and also for 20 steps at 24 px. Per conv layer, record the forward and backward kernel list, the time share of Triton elementwise/reduction kernels against cuDNN conv kernels, and the bytes read and written per BN/GELU kernel relative to the fp16 activation size, i.e. the number of passes over the activation. In the same profile, record per-layer conv time for group 2 (input for H2.13.2). For the scored row, rerun the E060 code unchanged as an extra family variance sample. Log the per-seed weight checksums (H4.4.1) and the cuDNN kernel names per layer and shape (H4.5.1).

expected: Time within 0.5% of E060 (4.65-4.70 s). Two-run pooled accuracy 0.7525-0.7550. A pool of 0.7540 or higher (H4 rule) makes it a zero-cost margin source and the new tip. If it lands within ±0.1 pp of 0.7531, it closes end-of-schedule tuning for Muon along with E057.
description: Base: E060 code. Apply Fable's tail at equal total steps. The Muon and SGD LR decay reaches its floor (0.05x for Muon, unchanged for SGD) about 4% of steps early and holds there until the end. Over the last ~8 steps, update a light final EMA every 4 steps (ema = 0.7*ema + 0.3*net with torch._foreach_lerp_, buffers allocated in build and reset in prepare). It replaces the end of the lookahead-EMA ramp, and evaluation uses those EMA weights, with BN buffers copied from the net. Change nothing else, and score it twice.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%, about 4.675 s). Two-run pooled accuracy 0.7520-0.7550. A pool of 0.7545 or higher supports H7.1.3 and becomes a margin source. A pool within ±0.15 pp of 0.7531 means the lr optimum transfers and Muon lr is closed on the bs-1536 tip. A pool of 0.7515 or lower means 0.24 is already at or above the optimum.
description: Base: E060 code. Change only the peak Muon LR of the conv filters from 0.24 to 0.28, through the existing 0-d tensor so nothing recompiles. The head keeps its own LR multiplier exactly as on the base, so the head's absolute LR also rises with the filter LR. With bs 1536 and only about 256 steps, the bs-1024 LR optimum (flat at 0.20-0.24, E034) may have shifted upward. Score it twice.
note: ideate: Stale base, and it is confounded with the head LR: on the E060 code the head's absolute LR would rise with the filter LR. Re-proposed on the E062 tip with the head's absolute LR held at 0.12, so only the filter LR changes.

expected: Time about 4.57-4.60 s: removing 0.25 of a 24 px epoch (~0.125 s at bs 1536) from E064/E065's 4.71 s gives -1.5 to -2% against the 4.669 s tip. Two-run pooled accuracy 0.7538-0.7550, i.e. about -0.05 to -0.12 pp against the E064/E065 pool of 0.7552, using the ~0.03-0.04 pp per 1% trim rate. If the pool is >=0.7540 (H4 rule), this becomes the new tip. If the pool is <=0.7530, the 24 px bridge is binding at 1.5 epochs and the reshuffle's accuracy gain cannot be resold as time.
description: Base: E064 code (a1aef09), which is the E062 tip (static shapes, max(dim).values pool, Muon floor 0.05, vectorized dirac, fused fp16 normalization, head Muon lr 0.5x) running E047's 2@16 + 1.5@24 + 4@32 schedule. Change only the length of the 24 px phase, from 1.5 to 1.25 epochs: 2@16 + 1.25@24 + 4@32 px, 7.25 total epochs, with step-indexed switches. Rescale the LR warmup/decay, Muon floor, EMA, lookahead and renorm cadence to the new total step count, the same way E047/E064 did. All shapes are already warmed up in build. Score it twice and log the source hash.

expected: Time about 4.57-4.60 s, about -2% against the tip. Removing half a 16 px epoch saves ~0.13 s, which is similar to the 24 px trim arm. Two-run pooled accuracy 0.7535-0.7552. If it is >=0.7540 and at least equal to the 24 px-trim arm's pool, the 16 px phase is the cheapest place to cut, and 1@16 + 1.5@24 + 4@32 comes next. A pool <=0.7525 supports H8: the early phase needs its update count.
description: Base: E064 code (a1aef09; 2@16 + 1.5@24 + 4@32 on the E062 tip). Trim the 16 px phase instead of the bridge: 1.5@16 + 1.5@24 + 4@32 px, 7.0 total epochs, with step-indexed switches. Rescale LR warmup/decay, Muon floor, EMA, lookahead and renorm to the new total step count as in E064. The warmup stays the same fraction of steps. Change nothing else and score it twice. This is the sister arm of the 24 px trim at about equal time. E064/E065 versus the tip showed that 24 px time buys accuracy at ~0.13 pp per 1% and 16 px time does not, so the 16 px phase may be the cheapest one to cut.

expected: Time within 0.5% of the tip (4.65-4.70 s). Two-run pooled accuracy 0.7525-0.7555 against the tip pool of 0.7537 (E062/E063/E067). A pool >=0.7550 (+0.13 pp) makes it a zero-cost margin source that can then be stacked onto the winning schedule trim. A pool within ±0.1 pp of 0.7537 closes end-of-schedule tuning for Muon, along with E057.
description: Rebased I074. Base: E062 code (the current tip, head Muon lr 0.5x). Apply Fable's tail at equal total steps. The Muon and SGD LR decay reaches its floor (0.05x for Muon, unchanged for SGD) about 4% of steps early and holds there until the end. Over the last ~8 steps, update a light final EMA every 4 steps (ema = 0.7*ema + 0.3*net via torch._foreach_lerp_; buffers allocated in build and reset in prepare). It replaces the end of the lookahead-EMA ramp, and evaluation uses those EMA weights with BN buffers copied from the net. Change nothing else, and score it twice.

description: Base: E062 code (head Muon lr 0.5x). Add decoupled weight decay to the Muon head weight [100, 576] only, at hiverge's bs-1536 scale: each step w -= lr_head_t * wd * w, with wd chosen so that wd*lr is about 1.6e-3 at peak, applied inside the compiled Muon update through a 0-d tensor so nothing recompiles. Leave the head bias, the filters and all schedules unchanged. Score it twice.

description: Rebased I075. Base: E062 code (head Muon lr 0.5x of filter lr). Change only the conv-filter peak Muon LR from 0.24 to 0.28 through the existing 0-d tensor. Keep the head's absolute peak LR at 0.12 (i.e. set its multiplier to 0.12/0.28) so that this run changes the filters only. Score it twice.

The prior is low (Muon lr was flat at 0.20-0.24 in E034, H7.1.3 confidence 0.10), and two scored runs on an obsolete base cannot be pooled against the current tip. expected: Scored row about 4.67 s, accuracy 0.752-0.755, which adds to the tip pool (currently 0.7537 over 3 runs). Profile prediction: 352 recovers <=60% of its FLOP-proportional group-2 time, while 320 recovers >=80%, i.e. tile misalignment explains E050's shortfall. If 320 also recovers <80%, width cuts are dead and H2.13 is refuted. If it recovers >=80%, a 320-width arm combined with the 2@16 + 1.5@24 reshuffle becomes worth one scored run.
description: Observational, untimed. On the E062 tip code, build three variants with group-2 widths 384, 352 and 320 (recompiled and warmed up in a side script). Use CUDA events and torch.profiler on 20 steps each at 32 px and 24 px, bs 1536. Record per-layer conv fwd/bwd time, elementwise time for group 2 and group 3's conv1, and total step time and energy (NVML). For the scored row, rerun the E062 code unchanged as a fourth tip-family variance sample (log weight checksums and source hash).

Accuracy within noise (two-run pool >=0.7525), since the math is equivalent up to fp16 rounding. If time drops <0.5%, or the opaque op breaks Inductor's conv-epilogue fusions and time rises, H2.16 is closed.
description: Explore. On the E062 tip code, replace BN(train) + GELU in the group-2 and group-3 blocks (32/24 px shapes only) with a custom torch.autograd.Function built from two Triton kernels. The forward computes per-channel stats with one reduction pass, then applies the BN affine and exact-erf GELU in one pass, saving only the fp16 pre-BN input and the per-channel mean/rstd. The backward recomputes the normalized value and GELU' on the fly in one fused reduction (dgamma, dbeta, sum terms) plus one apply pass. Register it so torch.compile treats it as an opaque op (allow_in_graph or a custom_op), and warm up every shape in build. Before scoring, check numerics against the compiled reference on one batch (max abs grad diff at fp16 level) and confirm the loss stays finite for 10 steps. Write down the predicted bytes moved per layer first.
note: H2.16.2 refuted

If the pool is 0.7550 or higher, this is the new tip at ~4.58 s with ~0.2 pp of margin to spend on the 32 px trim. If the pool is 0.7540 or lower, the tail and the reshuffle do not stack.

If it has the tail, do not run this; mark H2.10.4 refuted and go straight to the 32 px trim idea. If it lacks the tail, port the E068 tail unchanged, with all step counts rescaled to E070's total: LR decay reaches its floor at ~96% of steps and holds there; lookahead stops for the last ~8 steps; a final EMA lerp 0.3 runs every 4 steps (foreach_lerp, buffers allocated in build and reset in prepare); eval uses the EMA weights with BN buffers from the net. Change nothing else. Score it twice and log the source hash. Instrumentation: an untimed off-seed run of seeds 3-10 through the benchmark trial code, which also covers the H4.2.5 margin check.

E070/E071 therefore already measured tail + 2@16+1.25@24+4@32: pool 0.7537 -> tail and the 24 px trim do not stack to >= 0.7550 (H2.10.4 refuted as the idea instructs).

If the pool is 0.7540 or higher with the off-seed mean at 0.7530 or higher, this is the new tip. A loss of 0.3 pp or more means the 32 px tail is binding, and further cuts must come from elsewhere.
description: Gated on the tail-on-E070 idea reaching a pool of at least 0.7550. On that verified tail tip, cut the 32 px phase by 0.25 epoch: 2@16 + 1.25@24 + 3.75@32 px (7.0 ep), with a step-indexed switch. Rescale LR warmup/decay, the floor-hold point, the final-EMA window, lookahead and the renorm cadence to the new total step count, the same way E070 did. All shapes are already warmed up. Change nothing else. Score it twice, plus an untimed off-seed run of seeds 3-10. If the gate pool is only 0.7545-0.7550, cut 0.125 epoch instead (3.875@32).
note: Gate not met: requires a verified tail tip pool >= 0.7550 (or 0.7545 for the 0.125-epoch variant); the tail tip with the current schedule pools to 0.7537 (E070/E071), so the 32 px trim has no margin.

expected: Accuracy unchanged within noise (same math). Prediction: today trial 1 runs ≥0.5% slower than trials 2-3 (E069: 4.757 vs 4.708). The rehearsal removes that gap, so mean time drops 0.3-0.8% (~0.015-0.035 s). If trial 1 already matched trials 2-3 before the change and the mean time moves by less than 0.3%, H2.14.3 is refuted and lazy-init levers are closed.
description: Math-neutral. On the current tip code (the tail variant if banked, otherwise E070), add a full synthetic dress-rehearsal trial to build. Run prepare + the complete train loop on random uint8 data of the real shape: every phase, the resolution switches, the renorm on/off variants, the tail's floor-hold, the lookahead stop, the final-EMA foreach_lerp, the BN buffer copy, and eval at B=1024 and B=1. Then discard all state; prepare still resets everything. This warms the allocator pool, cuBLAS workspaces, cuDNN plans and any lazily compiled tail or EMA kernels that may currently first run inside timed trial 1. Log per-trial prepare/train times. Build stays well under 600 s (one synthetic trial is ~5 s). Score once.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Accuracy -0.1 to +0.15 pp vs the tip: the scored pool and the off-seed paired difference should both be at least +0.05 pp. A gain of +0.1 pp or more on both is margin for the 32 px trim. If 0.4x is 0.1 pp or more worse, the head optimum is at or above 0.5x and head lr is closed.
description: On the verified tail tip, change only the head's Muon lr multiplier from 0.5x to 0.4x of the filter lr. This is close to the spectral-condition value sqrt(100/576) ≈ 0.42. Set it through the head's own 0-d tensor so nothing recompiles. Decide with an untimed off-seed A/B on seeds 3-10 (tip vs 0.4x) plus two scored runs.

expected: Time within ±0.5%. Accuracy -0.3 to +0.3 pp. If both the off-seed mean and the scored pool beat the tip by 0.15 pp or more, MaxSup is a zero-cost margin source to spend on a trim. A difference within ±0.1 pp closes it. A loss of 0.2 pp or more means the 8-epoch regime needs LS's target-side regularization.
description: Explore. On the verified tail tip, replace label smoothing 0.3 with MaxSup: loss = CE(z, y) + 0.3*(max_k z_k - mean_k z_k), one fused op on the fp32-cast [B,100] logits inside the compiled train graph. Before scoring, smoke-test 10 steps for a finite loss under compile at every resolution. Change nothing else. Decide with an untimed off-seed run on seeds 3-10 plus two scored runs.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). If the final EMA carries the gain, accuracy falls 0.1-0.2 pp on both scored and off-seed, and EMA length and decay become the next tuning axis. If accuracy falls by 0.05 pp or less, the floor-hold or lookahead stop carries the gain, so the floor level should be tuned next. Info-only: no time gain expected.
description: Tail ablation on the verified tail tip, arm (a) only: remove the final EMA, so eval uses the net weights. Keep the floor-hold and the lookahead stop exactly as they are. Change nothing else. Run one scored run plus an untimed off-seed run of seeds 3-10, compared against the tip's off-seed mean. Arm (b), removing only the floor-hold, is queued only if arm (a) costs less than 0.05 pp.

expected: Time unchanged (4.57-4.61 s; a few extra foreach_lerp calls). E079 showed the 2-update final EMA is worth ~0.15-0.2 pp. A longer window that also averages iterates from before the floor-hold should add +0.05 to +0.15 pp: off-seed mean ~0.7535-0.7545 against a tip of ~0.7530, and a two-run scored pool of ~0.7540-0.7555 against 0.7537. If both instruments gain >=+0.1 pp, the result becomes the tip and funds the gated 32 px trim. A result within ±0.05 pp means the window length is saturated at 8 steps, so try the uniform-average arm next. If it is worse by >=0.1 pp, averaging over pre-floor iterates hurts at this LR.
description: Base: the current tip, E070 code (e945ed5). It is 2@16 + 1.25@24 + 4@32 px at 7.25 ep and already contains the Fable tail, as the I083 drop note confirms. Precondition, untimed: log the source hash and a one-line diff against e945ed5, so this run joins the right family (H4.2.4). Change only the final-EMA window. Start the final EMA 20 steps before the end instead of 8. Keep the cadence (every 4 steps) and the lerp (ema = 0.7*ema + 0.3*net via foreach_lerp), so there are ~5 updates instead of ~2. Initialize the EMA from the net weights at the window start, using buffers allocated in build and reset in prepare. Leave the floor-hold point (~96% of steps), the lookahead stop point, eval on the EMA weights and the BN buffers copied from the net all unchanged. This is a host-side step-index change only, so nothing new compiles. Decide with an untimed off-seed run on seeds 3-10. In the same session, rerun the tip off-seed so the baseline (0.7530) gets a second sample. Add two scored runs. Instrumentation for H4.4.1/H4.5.1: log per-seed final-weight checksums and the cuDNN conv kernel names per (layer, shape).

expected: Time unchanged (±0.6%). Accuracy +0.0 to +0.15 pp versus the tip, i.e. off-seed ~0.7530-0.7545. If it beats both the tip and the EMA-window arm by >=0.07 pp off-seed, a uniform weighting is the better averaging design for this ~236-step regime. If it is no better than the EMA-window arm, the averaging axis is closed after the winner of the two is banked.
description: Sibling arm of the EMA-window idea, sharing its off-seed tip baseline. Base: E070 code. Replace the final exponential EMA with a LAWA-style uniform average: take a snapshot of the net weights every 4 steps over the last 20 steps (5 snapshots), keep them as a running mean via foreach_lerp with weight 1/k for the k-th snapshot, and evaluate on the mean with the BN buffers copied from the net. The floor-hold and lookahead stop stay unchanged. Buffers are allocated in build and reset in prepare, and nothing recompiles. Change nothing else. Decide with an off-seed run on seeds 3-10 plus two scored runs, against the same tip off-seed baseline as the EMA-window idea.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.6%). This is a structural change to the effective-step schedule, so its effect may exceed the scalar knobs: off-seed and scored pool -0.2 to +0.3 pp. If the off-seed gain is >=+0.15 pp and the scored pool gains >=+0.1 pp, it becomes the tip with margin for a 32 px trim. If the off-seed delta is within ±0.1 pp, the implicit schedule is not binding and H9.1 is refuted. If accuracy drops >=0.2 pp, the late relative step under the tip's constant norm is already right for Muon+BN at ~236 steps.
description: Step 1 is free: read the filter-renorm code in the tip (E070 code) and log whether the target norm is constant or already decays. If it already decays, retire H9.1.1 and do not run this. Otherwise, change only the renorm target so it decays linearly from the tip's current value c to 0.157c over training, matching hiverge's 0.5012->0.0786 ratio. Compute it from progress inside the compiled Muon update as a 0-d GPU tensor, so nothing recompiles, and apply it on the existing renorm cadence (every 2+int(15*progress) steps). LR, floor, tail and everything else stay unchanged. Decide with an off-seed run on seeds 3-10 plus two scored runs.

expected: Time +1.5 to +3% (4.65-4.72 s). If bs 1536's accuracy cost (E038, ~0.13-0.3 pp) arose in the tail, accuracy rises +0.1 to +0.25 pp (off-seed ~0.754-0.755). That buys accuracy at >=0.055 pp per 1% of time and can fund a 32 px trim larger than its cost. If the gain is <=0.05 pp, the batch cost did not arise in the tail, and H2.11 is closed. This is an explore idea; it does not become the tip on its own because it is slower.
description: Base: E070 code. Keep bs 1536 for the 16 and 24 px phases, and run the 32 px phase (4 epochs) at bs 1024. Index LR warmup/decay, the floor-hold, the final-EMA window, lookahead and the renorm cadence by samples seen. The final-EMA window and lookahead stop stay at the same sample count as in the tip. Scale the SGD groups (BN biases, whitening bias, head bias) per phase by the E010 kilostep rule, and leave Muon lr and momentum unchanged. Compile the bs-1024 32 px train shape as a static graph and warm it up in build on synthetic data. Change nothing else. Pre-register the time cost: about +66 steps at 32 px. Decide with an off-seed run on seeds 3-10 plus two scored runs.

expected: Per-seed accuracy bit-identical or within noise. If the trial-1 window is pageable-staging overhead, trial-1 prepare falls from ~0.098 s to <=0.04 s, and trials 2-3 stay <=0.025 s (the extra host memcpy into pinned memory must not cost more than it saves). Mean time drops ~0.4-0.6% (~4.56 s). If trial-1 prepare stays >=0.08 s, the slow window is link- or driver-level (e.g. PCIe link power state), not pageable memory, and the line is closed. If trials 2-3 get slower by more than trial 1 saves, revert.
description: Math-neutral. Base: E070 code. In build, allocate an empty pinned host buffer (torch.empty(..., dtype=uint8, pin_memory=True)) and a GPU destination tensor of the training set's shape, with no real data. In prepare, copy the uint8 training array into the pinned buffer, upload it with non_blocking=True into the preallocated GPU tensor, and sync once before normalization. Change nothing else. Log per-trial prepare and train times. Score twice; decide on the per-trial prepare logs, not on the totals.

expected: Time about -2.3% (~-0.11 s, ~4.47 s) for the 0.125 cut, or ~-4.5% for the 0.25 cut. Accuracy -0.05 to -0.12 pp (-0.1 to -0.25 for the 0.25 cut), at the Muon full-res slope of ~0.54 pp/epoch. This is the first fractional 32 px trim on a Muon base, and it measures whether the tail is binding (H2.10.5). If the loss is <=0.05 pp per 1%, it is banked as the tip. If the loss is >=0.3 pp per 0.25 epoch, the 32 px phase is binding and cuts must come from elsewhere.
description: Gated. Run only after the EMA-window, uniform-average or renorm-decay idea yields a new tip whose off-seed mean is >=0.7540 and whose two-run scored pool is >=0.7547. On that tip, cut the 32 px phase by 0.125 epoch: 2@16 + 1.25@24 + 3.875@32 px (7.125 ep), with a step-indexed switch. Rescale LR warmup/decay, the floor-hold point, the final-averaging window, lookahead and the renorm cadence to the new total step count, the same way E070 did. All shapes are already warmed up in build. Change nothing else. Score twice, plus an off-seed run on seeds 3-10. If the gate tip has >=+0.2 pp of margin off-seed, cut 0.25 epoch (3.75@32) instead.
note: Gate not met: the EMA-window (E081), uniform-average (E083) and renorm-decay (E082) ideas all failed, so no tip with off-seed >= 0.7540 and pool >= 0.7547 exists to fund the 32 px trim.

expected: Time about 4.44-4.50 s, which is -1.5 to -2.7% against the tip's 4.565 s. E084 is ~4.68 s after the pinned-staging saving, and 0.25 epoch at 32 px with bs 1024 costs ~0.22 s. Two-run scored pool 0.7540-0.7550 and off-seed 0.7526-0.7538, i.e. -0.05 to -0.15 pp against E084. Even after the trim, the 32 px phase keeps ~45 more steps than the tip. Bank it as the new tip if the pool is >=0.7537, the off-seed mean is >=0.7525 and time is <=4.50 s. A loss of >=0.25 pp against E084 means the 32 px phase is binding even with more steps, so H2.10.5 is refuted for whole-phase trims.
description: Combine two near-misses: E084's bs-1024 32 px phase (+0.18 pp scored, +0.11 pp off-seed, +2.5% time) pays for the first fractional 32 px trim on a Muon base. Base: E084 code (3e30852, samples-indexed _fit, bs 1536 at 16/24 px, bs 1024 at 32 px) with E086's pinned staging buffer ported unchanged.
