The staging change is math-neutral and was confirmed bit-identical in E086/E087. Change only the length of the 32 px phase, from 4 to 3.75 epochs: 2@16 + 1.25@24 + 3.75@32 px (7.0 ep). The switch is indexed by samples seen. LR warmup/decay, the floor-hold, the final-EMA window, the lookahead stop and the renorm cadence are rescaled by samples, exactly as E084 did. All shapes are already warmed up in build. Precondition, untimed: log the source hash and a diff against 3e30852 plus 749bdce, so the run joins the right family (H4.2.4). Decide with an untimed off-seed run on seeds 3-10 plus two scored runs.

expected: 28 px epoch cost about 0.76-0.82x of a 32 px epoch. Time about 4.43-4.48 s (-2 to -3% against the tip), about equal to the trim arm. Accuracy -0.03 to -0.12 pp against the E084 pool, i.e. a scored pool of ~0.7543-0.7552 and off-seed ~0.7530-0.7538. H10's corollary predicts this beats the trim arm by >=0.05 pp at equal time, because it keeps every update. If it is no better than the trim arm, step count is not the currency in the tail, and resolution substitution is closed.
description: Equal-time sibling of the bs-1024 32 px trim idea, on the same base: E084 code plus the E086 pinned staging. Step 1, untimed: measure the compiled cost of a 28 px epoch at bs 1024 against a 32 px epoch at bs 1024 (2 epochs each, static shapes). If the ratio is >0.85x, drop the idea without a scored run. Step 2: replace the first 1.25 epochs of the 32 px phase with 28 px, using the same operator (flip + translate-2 at 32 px, then antialiased bilinear to 28 px; maps 27/13/6/3, max(dim).values pool). The schedule is 2@16 + 1.25@24 + 1.25@28 + 2.75@32 px. Samples seen are unchanged, so the step count is unchanged and LR/EMA/tail/renorm are untouched. Compile the bs-1024 28 px shape as a static graph and warm it up in build. Decide with an off-seed run on seeds 3-10 plus two scored runs, and compare against the trim arm.

expected: Time -0.3 to -1% (about 4.52-4.55 s), from removing the lookahead's per-step weight traffic about every 3 steps. Accuracy: off-seed within -0.05 pp of 0.7530 or better, and a scored pool of ~0.7525-0.7545. Bank it if both scored runs are faster than 4.561 s and the off-seed delta is >= -0.05 pp. If the off-seed loss is >=0.15 pp, lookahead still carries real smoothing under Muon at ~240 steps, and the line closes.
description: Base: the current tip (E086 code 749bdce: E070 schedule, Fable tail, pinned staging). Remove the SGD-era lookahead-EMA entirely, so the net trains on its own weights throughout. Drop its buffers and its foreach kernels from build and from the step loop. Keep the floor-hold, the final 8-step EMA (0.3 lerp every 4 steps), eval on the EMA weights and the BN buffers copied from the net. Change nothing else. Decide with an untimed off-seed run on seeds 3-10 against the tip's 0.7530, plus two scored runs; read the per-trial train-time logs.

expected: Time -0.3 to -0.7% (about 4.535-4.55 s). E061 saved ~0.3% by moving the freeze from 37.5% to 20% of steps, and this removes the remaining ~17% of steps that train the bias, all inside the cheap 16 px phase. Accuracy: off-seed within 0.1 pp of 0.7530 and a scored pool of 0.7525-0.7545. If the off-seed drop is >=0.15 pp, the 64x-LR bias needs more than 7 steps on CIFAR-100, so keep the current point. If the time drop is <0.2% over two runs, the whitening-bias lever is exhausted.
description: Base: the tip (E086 code). Precondition, free: log the current whiten_bias_epochs value in step terms. Then verify, in an untimed compiled-graph dump, that the steps after the detach have no stem dgrad or bias-reduction kernels. This was the H2.15.1 premise, and code reading says it is already present. Change only the freeze point. Train the whitening bias for the first 0.2 epoch (~7 steps at bs 1536), with its own LR tensor decaying linearly to 0 over that window (hiverge), then switch to the existing whiten_bias_grad=False graph for the rest of training. Both graph variants already exist and are warmed up for 16 px; the 24/32 px shapes need only the detached variant. Decide with an off-seed run on seeds 3-10 plus two scored runs.

expected: Scored row ~4.56 s, accuracy 0.752-0.755. Prediction: the sd of the off-seed mean across divergent reruns is 0.07-0.15 pp, so a paired off-seed A/B has SE ~0.1-0.2 pp, and the past verdicts at |d|<=0.18 (E077/E078/E079/E081/E084) are each <1.5 SE. If the sd is <0.05 pp, those verdicts stand and off-seed alone can decide future ideas. Every queued idea's pass bar gets re-scaled from this number.
description: Instrument calibration, with no recipe change. Rerun the unchanged tip (E086 code) on seeds 3-10 in at least 3 fresh processes through the benchmark's trial code. Each process rebuilds, so cuDNN benchmark picks are resampled. Continue until there are >=2 off-seed samples that are not bit-identical. Log the per-seed final-weight checksums (H4.4.1) and the cuDNN conv kernel names per (layer, shape) (H4.5.1). Report the sd of the 8-seed off-seed mean across the non-identical samples, and check whether the run means cluster by algorithm set. For the scored row, rerun the tip once; it adds a non-bit-identical tip sample if one occurs.

expected: Time equal to E084 within ±0.5% (~4.68 s). If update count is the mechanism, off-seed is 0.7538-0.7545 (within 0.05 pp of E084, gain >=+0.08 pp over the tip). If the gain falls to <=+0.03 pp against the tip, E084's effect came from the ~12-step window rather than the extra updates. In that case H2.11.3 is refuted as an update-count lever, and the trim arm built on E084 loses its funding rationale.
description: Ablation of E084's EMA-window confound. Base: E084 code plus the E086 pinned staging. Pin the final-EMA window and the lookahead stop to the tip's step counts (the last 8 steps, indexed from the end) instead of to equal sample counts, which gave ~12 steps at bs 1024. Change nothing else. Run one scored run and an off-seed run on seeds 3-10, compared against E084's off-seed 0.7541 and the tip's 0.7530. If the result is >= E084, use this window in the 32 px trim and 28 px arms that follow.

expected: Time +1 to +2.5% (about 4.61-4.68 s), since the low-res phases are per-step-bound at ~2 ms per step. Placement-independent prediction: off-seed +0.05 to +0.15 pp (0.7535-0.7545). A gain >=+0.2 pp means early steps are worth more, so the next time cut should keep early bs 1024 and cut elsewhere. A gain <=0 means steps matter only late, which favours the bs-1024 tail arms. Not a tip candidate on its own, because it is slower.
description: Placement test for update count. Base: the tip (E086 code), with the samples-indexed _fit from E084. Run bs 1024 in the 16 and 24 px phases only (~+53 steps), and keep the 32 px phase and the whole tail at bs 1536, so the final-EMA window stays at 8 steps. Index LR warmup/decay by samples, scale the SGD groups per phase by the kilostep rule, and leave Muon lr and momentum unchanged. Compile the bs-1024 16/24 px static shapes and warm them up in build. Decide with an off-seed run on seeds 3-10 plus one scored run, compared with E084 per added step.
note: ideate: Stale base: it targets E086 code, but the tip is E090 (bs-1024 28/32 px tail). Re-proposed unchanged in substance on E090, so its off-seed delta is measured against the current tip's calibrated off-seed baseline.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%, ~4.46 s). E081 showed a 20-step window costs ~0.09 pp against 8 steps, so interpolation puts the current ~12-step window at about -0.03 to -0.05 pp. Pinning should recover +0.03 to +0.10 pp: off-seed ~0.7530-0.7537 and a scored pool of ~0.7528-0.7540. It is banked as the tip if the off-seed delta is >= +0.03 pp and both scored runs are feasible. If the off-seed delta is <= 0, E084's +0.11 pp came from extra updates and not from the window, which supports H10 and leaves the window as it is.
description: I100 rebased onto the current tip. Base: E090 code (48b13a7): 2@16 + 1.25@24 at bs 1536, then 1.25@28 + 2.75@32 at bs 1024, with pinned staging and the Fable tail. Because the tip indexes by samples, the final-EMA window and the lookahead stop cover the same sample count as the bs-1536 tip, which is ~12 steps at bs 1024 (~3 EMA updates). Change only this: pin both to step counts measured from the end, so the final EMA covers the last 8 steps (lerp 0.3 every 4 steps, ~2 updates) and lookahead stops 8 steps before the end. The floor-hold point stays sample-indexed and unchanged. This is a host-side step-index change only and nothing recompiles. Precondition, untimed: log the source hash and a one-line diff against 48b13a7. Decide with an off-seed run on seeds 3-10 against the tip off-seed distinct mean (~0.7526, sd ~0.09 pp, E094), plus two scored runs. If it is accepted, use the pinned window in every later bs-1024-tail arm.

expected: Time 4.43-4.49 s (equal to the tip within ±0.6%). Accuracy +0.0 to +0.12 pp against the tip: off-seed ~0.7528-0.7538 and a scored pool of ~0.7525-0.7540. The bridge should gain ~+0.08-0.15 pp and the extra 28 px should cost ~-0.04 to -0.07 pp. If it is accepted (off-seed >= tip +0.05 pp, both scored runs feasible), it becomes the tip, and later time cuts come from more 32->28 substitution. If the off-seed delta is <= -0.05 pp, either the 24 px bridge gain was mostly noise or the 28 px substitution rate is steeper beyond 1.25 epochs. A follow-up that changes only one of the two halves would tell them apart.
description: Equal-time reallocation between two measured exchange rates. The 24 px bridge appears to buy ~0.13 pp per 1% (E064/E065 vs E070/E071, and the E070 trim cost ~0.14 pp per 1%). Substituting 28 px for 32 px costs only ~0.02 pp per 1% (E090: about -0.1 pp off-seed against E084 for -4.6% time). Base: E090 code. Change only the schedule to 2@16 + 1.5@24 (bs 1536) + 2@28 + 2@32 (bs 1024). Switches are indexed by samples. LR warmup/decay, the floor-hold, the final-EMA window, the lookahead stop and the renorm cadence are rescaled by samples exactly as E084/E090 do (samples rise by 0.25 epoch; steps rise by ~8). All shapes are already static and warmed up in build. Pre-registered time: +0.25 epoch at 24 px (~+0.125 s) and 0.75 epoch moved from 32 to 28 px (~-0.13 s), so equal time ±0.6%. Decide with an off-seed run on seeds 3-10 plus two scored runs.
note: H2.17 refuted

expected: Time +1.5 to +2.5% (about 4.53-4.57 s), because the low-res phases are per-step-bound at ~2 ms per step. Placement-independent prediction: off-seed +0.05 to +0.15 pp. A gain of >= +0.2 pp means early updates are worth more than late ones. A follow-up would then fund the early bs 1024 with more 32->28 substitution, at a net-better rate than the tip. A gain of <= 0 means updates only matter late, which closes early-phase batch levers. Not a tip candidate on its own, because it is slower.
description: I101 rebased onto the current tip (its old base, E086, is superseded). Base: E090 code, which already has the samples-indexed _fit. Run the 16 and 24 px phases at bs 1024 instead of 1536, which adds ~53 steps. The 28/32 px phases and the whole tail stay as on the tip. LR warmup/decay, the floor-hold and the renorm cadence are indexed by samples. Scale the SGD groups per phase by the kilostep rule and leave Muon lr and momentum unchanged. Compile static bs-1024 16/24 px shapes, including the whitening-bias-grad variant at 16 px, and warm them up in build. Decide with an off-seed run on seeds 3-10 plus one scored run. Compare the gain per added step with E084 (+0.11 pp off-seed for ~65 tail steps).

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Accuracy -0.15 to +0.15 pp. If the off-seed gain is >= +0.12 pp (about 1.3x the calibrated sd) and the scored pool is >= tip +0.05 pp, it is a free margin source and becomes the tip. If it is within ±0.1 pp, run 0.20 off-seed only once; if that is flat too, Muon lr is closed for good. A loss of >= 0.15 pp means 0.24 is at or above the optimum.
description: On the current tip (E090 code), change only the conv-filter Muon peak lr from 0.24 to 0.28 through its 0-d tensor. The head keeps its 0.5x multiplier, so its lr scales along, and nothing recompiles. The schedule shape, floor and tail are unchanged. Muon lr was only ever tuned at bs 1024 with ~384 steps on a pre-tail base (E034). The tip now has ~280 steps, mixed batch sizes and a floor-hold tail, so the optimum may have moved up. Decide with an off-seed run on seeds 3-10 against the tip's distinct mean, plus two scored runs.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Accuracy -0.15 to +0.15 pp. Removing the lookahead was costly, so a mild extension may add +0.05 to +0.1 pp. If the off-seed gain is >= +0.1 pp and the scored pool is >= tip, it becomes the tip and the opposite direction is not run. If it is <= -0.1 pp, the current horizon is at or past the optimum, and lookahead tuning closes after one shorter-horizon probe.
description: Explore the lookahead strength. E092 showed the SGD-era lookahead-EMA is worth ~0.2-0.3 pp under Muon (removing it cost -0.18 pp off-seed), but its strength was never tuned for Muon. Base: E090 code. Precondition, free: log the lookahead cadence and decay schedule in step terms for both batch-size phases. Change only the per-update decay base, so the effective averaging horizon is ~1.5x longer: for alpha_t = base^k * progress^p, set (1-base_new) = (1-base_old)/1.5. Cadence, the progress exponent, the stop point and the final EMA stay unchanged. This is a 0-d tensor or host-side constant and nothing recompiles. Decide with an off-seed run on seeds 3-10 plus two scored runs.
note: H6.8 refuted

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Low prior: uniform LS changes were null (E009, E037) and MaxSup lost 0.18 pp (E078). Expected -0.15 to +0.1 pp. Off-seed >= tip +0.12 pp would make phase-dependent LS a free margin source. A result within ±0.1 pp closes H6.7. A loss of >= 0.15 pp shows that LS's target-side term matters most at the end of training.
description: Explore in the TSLA direction, which the H6.7 re-scoping favours over lower early LS. Base: E090 code. Use label smoothing 0.3 for the first 80% of samples and 0.1 for the last 20%, which falls inside the 32 px phase and covers the floor-hold. Pass LS as a 0-d tensor into the compiled loss so the 32 px graph is not duplicated. If that is not possible, compile and warm both 32 px variants in build. Smoke-test 10 steps for a finite loss. Change nothing else. Decide with an off-seed run on seeds 3-10 plus one scored run, and a second scored run only if off-seed >= tip +0.1 pp.
note: H6.7 retired

expected: Scored row: a tip rerun at ~4.46 s and 0.751-0.754. Off-seed: under the BN-mismatch explanation, the loss against the tip shrinks to <= 0.1 pp. In that case, also averaging BN buffers in the current 8-step final EMA is a candidate free gain worth one A/B. If the loss stays >= 0.2 pp, averaging higher-LR pre-floor iterates is the cause, and end-of-run averaging closes for good.
description: Mechanism test, run off-seed only. On the current tip code (E090), replace the final EMA with E083's LAWA (a uniform mean of 5 snapshots every 4 steps over the last 20 steps). Also average the BN running_mean/running_var buffers over the same snapshots with the same 1/k running-mean lerp, instead of copying them from the final net. Buffers are allocated in build and reset in prepare. Run seeds 3-10 off-seed in an untimed side script and compare with E083's -0.29 pp loss against the tip. For the scored row, rerun the unchanged tip E090 code once, which adds a distinct tip sample to the thin tip pool (currently ~0.7524 over two distinct runs).
note: ideate: Its comparator, E083's -0.29 pp, was measured on E070-era code against a different tip baseline, and it uses seeds 3-10 (SE ~0.1-0.13 pp), so it cannot cleanly separate the two H6.5 mechanisms. Superseded by the new H6.5.4 idea, which follows the hypothesis spec (20-step EMA with BN buffers lerped) on E090 with the seeds 3-26 paired baseline.

expected: Scored row: ~4.46 s (±0.5%), accuracy 0.751-0.754. Off-seed: per-seed sd 0.22-0.38 pp, so the 24-seed SE is ~0.05-0.08 pp. E090 mean 0.7518-0.7530 and E095 mean 0.7535-0.7548, a gap of +0.1 to +0.2 pp. If E090 is >=0.7535, it counts as robustly banked and the pressure to add accuracy drops. If E095-E090 is <0.05 pp, the 28 px substitution was nearly free and further 32->28 substitution is reopened. No time change.
description: Instrument and tip decision, with no recipe change. In untimed side scripts, run the unchanged E090 code (48b13a7) and the unchanged E095 code (0503e38) through the benchmark's own trial code on seeds 3-26: 24 seeds each, one fresh process per config so the cuDNN picks are resampled. Do not edit benchmark/. Log per-seed accuracy, per-seed final-weight checksums, and the cuDNN conv kernel names per (layer, shape) from the profiler in build and the first steps; this is the free by-product for H4.5.1. For the scored row, rerun E090 unchanged; a non-bit-identical result adds a third distinct tip sample. Store both 24-seed per-seed vectors as the paired baselines for every later off-seed A/B on seeds 3-26.

expected: At least one 24/28/32 px conv shape picks a different kernel. Mean time -0.3 to -1.5% (about 4.40-4.45 s), mostly in the energy-bound 28/32 px phases. Build +10 to +60 s. Accuracy is math-equivalent within noise: distinct pool within 0.1 pp of the E090 family (~0.752-0.754). If the kernel names are identical to the defaults, or the time change is <0.3%, close the lever. If it is banked, it stacks on any later tip and also transfers to the PCIe judge, since it is per-kernel efficiency.
description: Math-neutral FLOP-free time lever. Base: E090 code. At the very start of build, before any conv runs, set torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark_limit = 0 so that cuDNN v8 tries every available algorithm for each static train shape (16/24 px at bs 1536, 28/32 px at bs 1024, both whitening-bias-grad variants) and for the eval path, instead of the default 10. Change nothing else. Log the build time, which must stay <600 s, the per-phase epoch times, and the conv kernel names per (layer, shape), and diff the kernel names against the E090 defaults logged by the H4.2.7 run. Score twice and compare distinct samples against the E090 family.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%, ~4.46 s). Path-length prediction: off-seed +0.05 to +0.12 pp (E090 gave back ~0.15-0.25 pp of 32 px exposure against E095, and more movement per 32 px step should recover part of it). A pass (off-seed >= +0.08 pp and a distinct scored mean >=0.7535) makes it the robust tip at ~4.46 s. If the gain is <= +0.03 pp, update count rather than movement is the mechanism, and only per-phase batch size (H2.11) remains. If the loss is >=0.1 pp, the late Muon lr is already at or above its optimum.
description: Path-length test, run directly on the tip so a positive result is immediately bankable. Deviation from the H10.2.1 text: it uses the E090 base instead of E086, so it reuses the seeds 3-26 E090 baseline from the H4.2.7 run and needs no new control. Base: E090 code. In the 32 px phase only (the final 2.75 epochs at bs 1024, floor-hold included), multiply the conv-filter Muon lr schedule by 1.25 (0.24 -> 0.30 at the same schedule position). The head keeps its 0.5x multiplier and scales along. The 16/24/28 px phases are unchanged. Implement it as a phase-keyed host-side factor written into the existing 0-d lr tensor, so nothing recompiles. Decide on off-seed seeds 3-26, paired against the E090 baseline, plus two distinct scored samples.

expected: Time +0.3 to +0.8% (~4.48-4.50 s; the stem dgrad comes back for ~29% more of the samples). Adaptation prediction: off-seed +0.05 to +0.15 pp, with the bias changing by >=10% of its norm after the 28 and 32 px switches. A gain of >=0.1 pp beats the 0.065 pp per 1% bar and, with two feasible scored samples, makes it the tip. If the change is within ±0.05 pp and the bias barely moves after the switches, the freeze point is closed and E093's loss was early-phase fragility.
description: Resolution-statistics adaptation test (the 70% arm). Base: E090 code. Move the whitening-bias detach point from ~41% of samples (inside the 24 px phase) to ~70% of samples (inside the 32 px phase, after both the 28 and 32 px switches). Keep the bias LR schedule otherwise unchanged. Warm up the whiten_bias_grad=True graph variants for the 24 px bs-1536, 28 px bs-1024 and 32 px bs-1024 shapes in build on synthetic data. Change nothing else. Log the whitening-bias vector norm and its relative change across each resolution switch. Decide on off-seed seeds 3-26, paired against the E090 baseline, plus two distinct scored samples.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). BN-mismatch explanation: off-seed >= E090 +0.05 pp (against E081's -0.09 with copied buffers). Iterate-LR explanation: off-seed <= E090 -0.05 pp. If the BN explanation wins by >=0.08 pp, a follow-up adds BN-buffer averaging to the 8-step window as a free gain. If the iterate-LR explanation wins, end-of-run averaging and H6 close.
description: Discriminating test for end-of-run averaging, matching the H6.5.4 spec on the current tip. Base: E090 code. Replace the 8-step final EMA with E081's 20-step window (lerp 0.3 every 4 steps from 20 steps before the end, initialized from the net at the window start). Also lerp every BN running_mean/running_var buffer with the same weights, in the same foreach_lerp, instead of copying the buffers from the final net. EMA buffer copies are allocated in build and reset in prepare. The lookahead stop and floor-hold are unchanged, and nothing recompiles. Decide on off-seed seeds 3-26, paired against the E090 baseline. Add one scored run, and a second only if off-seed is >= +0.05 pp.

expected: Projection: group-3 conv3 removal saves ~5-8% of run time (576-ch 3x3 GEMMs plus ~23 elementwise kernels, small maps). Group-1 conv3 removal saves ~4-7% (large 31x31 maps, elementwise-heavy). If either is >=6%, queue a scored arm that spends half the saving on extra 32 px samples (net ~-3%). If both are <6%, depth cuts close without a scored run. Scored row ~4.46 s, 0.751-0.754.
description: Explore depth cuts, untimed first. In a side script on E090 code, build two variants with recompile and warm-up: (a) group-1 conv3 removed and (b) group-3 conv3 removed. Muon stacks are re-batched for the changed filter counts. Measure per-step time with CUDA events and NVML energy over 20 steps each at 32 px bs 1024, 28 px bs 1024, 24 px bs 1536 and 16 px bs 1536, then project total run time over the E090 schedule. For the scored row, rerun E090 unchanged (another distinct tip sample). Score a depth variant later only if its projection shows >=6%.

expected: Time ~4.46 s (±0.5%). Scored accuracy 0.751-0.756. Pooled off-seed mean for E100 0.7518-0.7530, with process-to-process sd of the 24-seed mean ~0.05-0.12 pp. If the pooled distinct scored mean (3 samples) is >=0.7535, E100 counts as robustly banked. If it is <0.7530, E100 is feasible by luck like E090, and the next zero-time accuracy lever must land before any time cut. If kernel-name sets cluster with process means (>=0.2 pp apart), H4.5.1 is supported.
description: Instrument run with no recipe change, and the baseline for every following idea. The tip is E100 code (176e5ec). Its two distinct scored samples are 0.7561 and 0.7516, and its only off-seed sample is one process (22 seeds, 0.7523). E098 showed that one process per arm cannot resolve 0.1 pp. In an untimed side script, run the unchanged E100 code through the benchmark's own trial code on seeds 3-26 in 2 more fresh processes, so cuDNN picks are resampled. Do not edit benchmark/. Log per-seed accuracy, per-seed final-weight checksums and the cuDNN conv kernel names per (layer, shape); the kernel names are the free by-product for H4.5.1. For the scored row, rerun E100 unchanged; a non-bit-identical result adds a third distinct scored sample. Store the pooled 24-seed vectors (>=2 distinct processes) as the paired baseline for every later off-seed A/B.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%, ~4.46 s). Path-length prediction: off-seed +0.06 to +0.12 pp over E100, i.e. most of E104's gain for free. If it passes (pooled off-seed >= +0.08 pp and a distinct scored mean >=0.7540), it becomes the tip and funds a ~1-1.5% 32 px trim. If the gain is <= +0.03 pp, E104's gain was update count, and only the per-step-cost batch route remains. A loss of >=0.1 pp means early Muon steps are already at the stability edge (the 64x-LR SGD biases are not touched, so the loss would be attributable to the filters).
description: Placement-paired test of the path-length mechanism in the low-res phases. E104 bought ~+0.12 pp off-seed by running the 16/24 px phases at bs 1024, i.e. ~1.5x more Muon steps there, at +2.8% time. If the gain is Muon path length (lr × steps) rather than update count, a 1.5x larger Muon lr in those phases should reproduce it at zero time. Base: E100 code. In the 16 and 24 px phases only (bs 1536, warmup included), multiply the conv-filter Muon lr schedule by 1.5 (0.24 -> 0.36 at the same schedule position). The head keeps its 0.5x multiplier and scales along. The SGD groups, the 28/32 px phases (32 px keeps its 1.25x) and the tail are unchanged. Implement it as a phase-keyed host-side factor written into the existing 0-d lr tensor, so nothing recompiles. Before scoring, smoke-test that the 16 px loss stays finite over the first 30 steps. Decide on off-seed seeds 3-26 in >=2 fresh processes, paired against the E100 baseline, plus two distinct scored samples.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). If path length is still below its optimum, off-seed +0.04 to +0.10 pp over E100, and the factor becomes the tip setting. If the result is within ±0.04 pp, the optimum is near 1.25-1.5, so keep 1.25 (simpler). If it is <= -0.08 pp, 1.25 was at or past the optimum, and E100's gain might partly be noise; H10.2 confidence then drops. Dose-response monotonicity (1.0 -> 1.25 -> 1.5) is the key evidence for the mechanism.
description: Dose-response on the one weakly supported zero-time lever. E100 multiplied the 32 px-phase filter Muon lr by 1.25 (+0.09 pp off-seed, distinct scored mean 0.7538). Base: E100 code. Change only that 32 px-phase factor, from 1.25 to 1.5 (0.36 at the same schedule position; the floor-hold covers the same samples, at 1.5x). The head keeps 0.5x and scales along. Nothing else changes, and the phase-keyed 0-d tensor means nothing recompiles. Decide on off-seed seeds 3-26 in >=2 fresh processes against the E100 baseline, plus two distinct scored samples.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Prediction: off-seed +0.03 to +0.08 pp, smaller than E100's +0.09 because the 28 px phase has fewer samples than the 32 px phase. A pass (>= +0.06 pp off-seed with distinct scored mean >= base) makes it the tip setting. A result within ±0.04 pp means the late gain is specific to the 32 px phase, which supports H11's test-resolution exposure over generic late path length.
description: Extend E100's path-length factor to the other bs-1024 phase. In E100 only the 32 px phase got the 1.25x Muon lr. The 1.25-epoch 28 px phase also runs at bs 1024 and is part of the late, test-adjacent training that H11 calls binding. Base: E100 code. In the 28 px phase only, multiply the conv-filter Muon lr schedule by 1.25. The head scales along. The 16/24 px phases, the 32 px factor (1.25) and the tail are unchanged. This is a phase-keyed host-side factor, so nothing recompiles. Decide on off-seed seeds 3-26 in >=2 fresh processes against the E100 baseline, plus two distinct scored samples. If the low-res-lr idea (H10.2) passes first, rebase onto it.

expected: Time unchanged or -0.1% (one fewer gather in late batches). Accuracy -0.1 to +0.12 pp. If off-seed is >= +0.08 pp, late augmentation annealing is a free margin source and H11(b) gains support; the next step is tuning the anneal point (8-20%). If off-seed is <= -0.08 pp, translate regularization still matters at the end (consistent with LS 0.3 being optimal), and this line closes.
description: Explore H11's mechanism (b): late training on test-like inputs is what binds. Base: E100 code. For the last ~12% of samples (inside the 32 px phase, covering the floor-hold and final EMA), turn off the translate-2 augmentation, keeping the alternating flip, so late training sees un-shifted 32 px images like the test set. This is a host-side flag in the GPU augmentation; the net graph is unchanged, and if the augment op is compiled, warm both variants in build. E008 showed short schedules under-fit, so less late augmentation may help. Change nothing else. Decide on off-seed seeds 3-26 in >=2 fresh processes against the E100 baseline, plus one scored sample and a second only if off-seed >= +0.05 pp.
note: H11 retired

expected: No time or accuracy change (scored row ~4.46 s, 0.751-0.756). Prediction: projected PCIe times are ~1.15-1.3x local, and the E095-vs-E100 gap widens by >=1.1x, because the extra 32 px work is energy-bound. Use the projection only to break ties between configs within 3% locally. Depth cuts, as FLOP and byte levers, should project at least as well as they measure locally.
description: Free, untimed analysis with no scored-path change. The judge is a 300 W A100 PCIe. Using existing NVML/phase logs (E045 onward; add a short NVML capture in the E100 rerun if the logs lack per-phase energy), project the judge time of E095, E090/E096 and E100 as the sum over phases of max(phase energy / 300 W, phase GPU-busy time). Also project the two depth-cut variants once I114 has measured them. Report the projected ranking and the gap ratios against the local times. For the scored row, if one is required, rerun E100 unchanged (an extra distinct sample).
note: ideate: Low information. It is a tie-breaker projection only, the existing NVML logs lack the per-phase energy for most configs, and I114's untimed profile already records NVML energy for the variants that matter. With E100 robustly banked, no local tie within 3% is pending that would need this.

expected: Time +0.3 to +0.9% (~4.48-4.51 s). The H8 prediction is a pooled off-seed gain of >= +0.1 pp and a distinct scored mean >= 0.7543. My central estimate is -0.05 to +0.10 pp, because E104 suggests added steps buy about the same anywhere, and this run moves samples rather than adding steps. A gain of >= +0.1 pp at <1% time beats every measured exchange rate. It would become the tip, and its margin would fund a ~1.5% 32 px trim. A result of <= -0.05 pp refutes N8.2 in favour of H11, which closes bridge lengthening.
description: Equal-time reallocation from the 32 px phase into the 24 px bridge. This is the direct discriminating test between H8.2 (the bridge is worth ~0.13 pp per 1%) and H11 (late full-resolution training is what binds). Base: E100 code (176e5ec). If I116 (low-res Muon lr x1.5) is banked first, rebase onto it and say so in the log. Change only the schedule: 2@16 + 1.75@24 at bs 1536, then 1.25@28 + 2.5@32 at bs 1024 (was 1.25@24 and 2.75@32). Total samples stay at 7.5 epochs. Resolution switches, LR warmup/decay, the floor-hold, the renorm cadence and the 32 px-phase Muon factor (1.25x) are indexed by samples, as in E100. The final-EMA window and lookahead stop stay pinned to the last 8 steps. All shapes are already static and warmed up in build. Precondition, untimed: log the source hash and a one-line diff against 176e5ec. Pre-registered time: +0.5 epoch at 24 px (~+0.26 s) minus 0.25 epoch at 32 px/bs 1024 (~-0.23 s) gives +0.3 to +0.9%. Decide on off-seed seeds 3-26 in >=3 fresh processes, paired against the pooled E106 baseline, plus two distinct scored samples.

expected: Time within ±0.3%, since a single argsort per epoch costs nothing measurable. Expected accuracy 0 to +0.10 pp. The pass bar is a pooled off-seed gain of >= +0.1 pp with a distinct scored mean >= 0.7543. A pass would make it a free margin source stackable on any tip and funding a ~1.5% 32 px trim. A result within ±0.05 pp closes H12.2. A loss of >= 0.1 pp would mean the batch-to-batch class variance acts as useful noise in this ~280-step regime.
description: Class-balanced (stratified) minibatches at zero compute. Base: E100 code. Inside train, at the start of each epoch, build the permutation on the GPU from the global RNG, which the harness seeds per trial. Nothing is built at import or in build. Steps: (1) for each of the 100 classes, shuffle its 500 indices into a [500, 100] (rank, class) index matrix, using one argsort of random keys within class-sorted labels; (2) independently permute the class order within each rank row; (3) flatten row-major. Every consecutive block of 100 then contains each class exactly once, so a bs-1536 batch holds 15-16 images per class and a bs-1024 batch holds 10-11. The class-sorted label index is computed in prepare, which is timed. Samples, steps, shapes and augmentation are unchanged, and the net graph is untouched. Untimed check: the per-batch class-count max-min is <=1 and the epoch covers all 50,000 images exactly once. Decide on off-seed seeds 3-26 in >=3 fresh processes, paired against the E106 pooled baseline, plus two distinct scored samples.

expected: Most likely outcome: the logs show tile padding on 128-wide tiles (E080: 352/320 recovered only 33-60% of their FLOP savings). Then 640 projects at +0.5 to +1.5% time and 512 at <=-2%, which refutes the 'saves more than FLOP share' half. If 640 is scored, expect +0.05 to +0.15 pp off-seed (capacity is valuable on CIFAR-100: E005, E017), which beats the 0.065 pp per 1% bar when the cost is <=1.5%. If the kernels use 64-wide tiles, H2.19 closes for free.
description: Group-3 width set by tile alignment, decided cheaply first. Step 1, free: read the cuDNN/cutlass kernel names already logged for the group-3 convs at 28/32 px bs 1024 and 24 px bs 1536 (E094/E098/E099/E106 profiler logs). If every group-3 GEMM uses a tile width dividing 576 (64-wide N/M tiles), close H2.19 with no run. Step 2, untimed, only if 128/256-wide tiles appear: in a side script on E100 code, build group-3 widths 512, 576 and 640. Group-3 conv1 input stays 384, the head becomes [100, W], and the Muon stacks are re-batched. Compile and warm up all shapes. Measure ms/step and NVML energy over 20 steps per (resolution, batch) shape, and project total run time over the E100 schedule. Step 3: score 640 on E100 only if it projects <=+1.5% total time. Decide on off-seed seeds 3-26 in >=3 fresh processes against E106, plus two distinct scored samples. If no scored arm is justified, the scored row reruns E100 unchanged as an extra distinct tip sample.

expected: Time within ±0.5%. Explore idea with a low-to-moderate prior: Fort et al. report gains on CIFAR-100 at long schedules, but here 32 px exposure appears to bind (E088/E090). Central estimate -0.15 to +0.05 pp off-seed. A pooled gain of >= +0.1 pp would open a whole augmentation-multiplicity axis, including 4 copies and moving it into earlier phases. A result of <= -0.15 pp shows that unique-image coverage dominates at ~7 epochs and closes H12.1.
description: Multi-sample augmentation in the 32 px phase, at equal compute. Base: E100 code. In the 2.75-epoch 32 px phase only (bs 1024), build each batch from 512 unique images, drawn as the next 512 of the epoch permutation, times 2 augmentation draws. Copy A keeps the existing alternating-flip state and its own translate offsets. Copy B gets the opposite flip and independently drawn translate offsets. Batch shape, step count, LR/EMA/tail indexing and the compiled graphs are unchanged; only the gather indices and the augmentation parameters differ. The 32 px phase then covers ~1.375 unique epochs instead of 2.75. The 16/24/28 px phases are unchanged. Smoke-test that the duplicated indices and the flip parity are correct on one batch. Decide on off-seed seeds 3-26 in >=3 fresh processes against E106, plus one scored sample, and a second only if off-seed >= +0.05 pp.

expected: Scored row ~4.46-4.48 s, accuracy 0.751-0.756. Instrument: per-seed sd of the paired difference 0.3-0.5 pp, so the 100-seed SE is 0.03-0.05 pp, and the mean A-B difference stays within ±2 SE of 0. That sets the support/refute bar for H8.2.2, H12.x and H2.20 at ~2x the observed SE (~0.08 pp). If the paired-difference sd is <0.15 pp, seed pairing is strong and the 22-seed verdicts can stand. About 15-20 min of untimed GPU time.
description: Calibrate the large-seed paired instrument. Nothing changes in the scored path. In an untimed side script, run the benchmark's own trial code (benchmark/ is not edited) on seeds 3-102 for two arms, one fresh process each. Arm A is unchanged E100 code (176e5ec). Arm B is E100 plus one math-neutral perturbation that does change fp bits: in prepare, compute the normalization as x*inv_std - mean*inv_std instead of (x-mean)*inv_std, which re-draws every seed's trajectory. Log per-seed accuracy, per-seed final-weight checksums and the cuDNN conv kernel names per (layer, shape). Free by-product for H4.5.1: in the same session, cluster the kernel-name sets already logged in E094/E098/E099/E106 against their process means. Store arm A's 100-seed vector as the paired baseline for every later large-seed A/B, so H8.2.2 needs only its treatment arm. Scored row: rerun E100 unchanged, which adds a 4th distinct scored sample.

expected: No time change in the scored row (~4.47 s). Paired gain of E108 over E100: central estimate +0.03 to +0.08 pp (E108's 3-process off-seed was +0.09). If it is >= +0.08 pp (~2 SE), H8.2 is supported. The follow-up is then 2@16 + 2.0@24 + 1.25@28 + 2.25@32, judged on whether the bridge gain funds a ~1.5% net 32 px trim (target ~4.40 s). If it is <= -0.05 pp, H11 wins, H8.2 is refuted and bridge lengthening closes. Anything in between leaves both at ~0 and closes the reallocation axis as not worth it.
description: Decisive test of bridge versus tail on the large-seed instrument. Run E108 code (340ecc1: 2@16 + 1.75@24 at bs 1536, then 1.25@28 + 2.5@32 at bs 1024, everything else as E100) untimed through the benchmark trial code on seeds 3-102, one fresh process. Pair it per seed against the E100 vector from the H4.6.1 calibration run. Gate: run only after H4.6.1 has produced its baseline and SE. Precondition, untimed: log the source hash and a one-line diff against 176e5ec. Scored row: rerun E100 unchanged, which adds another distinct gate sample (also useful to H4.8).

expected: Profile: the detached step is 10-18% cheaper at 32 px. Group 1 works on the largest maps (31x31x128), so its backward conv plus elementwise work is a large share of the energy-bound step. Scored freeze from 85%: time -2.5 to -4% (about 4.29-4.36 s). Accuracy loss 0 to -0.1 pp paired, because group 1 barely moves at the floor LR. If the loss is <=0.1 pp, the rate is <=0.035 pp per 1%, it becomes the tip, and a 70% freeze is tried next. If the profiled saving is <6%, close H2.20 without a scored run. If the paired loss is >=0.15 pp, early layers still adapt at the end, as E093 suggests, and the line closes.
description: Late freeze of group 1 plus the stem as a FLOP/byte time lever, profiled untimed first. Step 1, untimed side script on E100 code: build a second static 32 px / bs-1024 train graph in which group 1's output is detached (no backward into group 1 or the stem; group-1 BN still runs in train mode). Warm it up in build. Measure ms/step and NVML energy over 20 steps for each variant, and project total run time for freezes over the last 15% and last 30% of samples. Step 2, only if the detached step is >=8% cheaper: score a freeze from 85% of samples, which lies inside the 32 px phase and covers the floor-hold and final EMA. From then on, group-1 filters drop out of the compiled Muon stacks (a second warmed variant of the update, with momentum untouched) and group-1 BN params drop out of the SGD foreach. Lookahead and the final EMA stay unchanged. Selection is a host-side flag, so nothing recompiles in timed code. Decide accuracy on the large-seed paired instrument (H4.6.1) against E100, plus two distinct scored samples.
note: E115 crashed: fix and relaunch, or drop it

expected: Scored row ~4.47 s, 0.751-0.756. Central prediction (luck): pooled E100 seeds-0-2 mean ~0.7530-0.7540 and pooled E100 - E090 within ±0.1 pp, converging toward their off-seed means. In that case the local gate passes ~50-60% of the time at zero population margin, and the next time cut needs ~+0.1 pp of accuracy funded first. If E100 - E090 is >= +0.15 pp on seeds 0-2 while off-seed stays ~0, the offset is persistent, and gate decisions should weight seeds 0-2 directly. For H4.7.1: if the side-script process sd of the 3-seed mean is <0.08 pp while scored samples spread 0.45 pp, the side script differs from the harness, and off-seed verdicts do not transfer to the gate.
description: Gate-instrument question: is E100's seeds-0-2 advantage a persistent recipe x seed offset or luck? In an untimed side script that uses the benchmark's own trial code, run E100 (176e5ec) and E090 (48b13a7) on seeds 0-2 in 5 fresh processes each, alternating arms so time-of-day effects cancel. Log per-seed accuracy, per-seed final-weight checksums and kernel-name sets. The same data answers H4.7.1: compare the spread of the side-script E100 3-seed means with the distinct scored samples (0.7561/0.7516/0.7551). Scored row: rerun E100 unchanged.
note: H4.8 retired

expected: E116 population mean 0.7518-0.7524, i.e. -0.07 to -0.12 pp vs the pooled E100 baseline (0.7530). That predicts an official 40-seed mean of ~0.752, which clears 0.75 almost surely. Each scored attempt passes with probability ~0.4-0.5, so P(>= 1 pass in 3) ~0.8. Scored time 4.26-4.31 s, about -3.5 to -4.5% vs the 4.465 s tip, which would be the largest single time gain since E090. If the population mean is < 0.7515, the 85% freeze cannot be banked without an accuracy source, and the 92% point becomes the candidate. Caveat: a passing scored row is partly luck by construction. The banking decision rests on the population mean, not on the passing row.
description: Bank the E116 late freeze under the H4.9 acceptance rule. The code is E116 unchanged (82e6219: stem and group 1 detached from 85% of samples, all renorm x freeze variants warmed in build). Step 1, untimed: run E116 through the benchmark's own trial code on seeds 103-202 in one fresh process, which brings E116 to ~198 distinct trajectories. Compare its pooled mean with the pooled 200-trajectory E100 baseline (E113 arms A+B, H4.6.2; SE ~0.026 pp). Step 2: score E116 code up to 3 times. Stop at the first scored row >= 0.753. Log per-trial prepare/train times in every scored run to explain the 4.306 s scored vs 4.263 s dev gap (e.g. trial-1 first use of the frozen variant). Bank E116 as the tip only if its population mean is >= 0.7518 and a scored row >= 0.753 appears within 3 attempts. Otherwise E100 stays the tip and the freeze needs funding (I_b / H10.1.2).

expected: Time about -1.8 to -2.4% vs E100 (~4.36-4.39 s), roughly half of E116's saving, since about half as many 32 px samples are frozen. Accuracy -0.02 to -0.06 pp vs the pooled baseline (population mean ~0.7524-0.7528), i.e. <= 0.03 pp per 1%. If the loss is <= 0.03 pp, the cost of freezing is concentrated in the 85-92% window (convex dose-response), and 92% is the safer bankable point under H4.9. If the loss is ~0.06 pp or more (similar to 85%), the cost is a fixed 'any freeze' penalty and 85% dominates.
description: Dose-response point at a later freeze. Base: E116 code. Change only the freeze point of stem + group 1, from 85% to 92% of samples. That point is still inside the 32 px / bs-1024 phase and covers the floor-hold and the final 8-step EMA. Keep every graph and Muon-stack variant as in E116, warmed in build. Before scoring, verify with TORCH_LOGS=recompiles on a 2-trial dev run that nothing recompiles after build. Accuracy is decided untimed on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process against the pooled 200-trajectory E100 baseline. Add two distinct scored samples with per-trial time logs.

expected: Paired gain +0.04 to +0.12 pp (E104's 8-seed estimate was +0.12, ~1 SE). If it is >= +0.08 pp (~2.5 SE), update count buys ~0.03-0.04 pp per 1% of time. Then 'bs 1024 everywhere + 75% freeze' becomes a candidate tip: about -4 to -5% time net, with accuracy near E100. If it is <= +0.04 pp, the rate is not real, H10 loses its only support, and the freeze can only be funded by later freeze points. Scored row ~4.30 or ~4.47 s depending on the tip, 0.751-0.756.
description: Measure the update-count rate before using it to fund the freeze. Untimed, through the benchmark trial code: run E104 code (594b48e: bs 1024 in the 16/24 px phases as well, ~+53 steps, everything else as E100) on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process. Compare it with the pooled 200-trajectory E100 baseline (SE ~0.032). No scored change is needed for the decision. For the scored row, rerun the current tip unchanged; if E116 is banked, that rerun adds a distinct E116 gate sample.

expected: Stem + group 1 take >= 17% of backward GPU time/energy, against a ~13% backward-FLOP share (ratio >= 1.3x), and the detached step is 15-20% cheaper, which would support H2.21. The BN/GELU backward on the 31x31x128 maps should make up most of the excess. In that case a group-1 width profile (H2.21.2) and the deeper freeze (H2.20.4) are worth running. If the ratio is < 1.1x, E116's saving comes from elsewhere (e.g. removed optimizer work for group-1 params), N_bytes is refuted, and group-1 width closes without a run. Scored row ~4.3-4.47 s, 0.751-0.756.
description: Untimed per-group backward energy profile on E100 at 32 px / bs 1024 (static graphs, warmed in build), with no change to the scored path. Use CUDA events plus torch.profiler over 20 steps for the full step and for the E116 detached variant. Attribute backward kernel time to stem, group 1, group 2, group 3 and the head (conv dgrad/wgrad, BN/GELU backward reductions and applies). Record bytes read and written per BN/GELU backward kernel and NVML energy per step. Also read the logged cuDNN kernel tile shapes for the group-1 convs, which is the free first step of H2.21.2. For the scored row, rerun the current tip unchanged (an extra distinct gate sample).

expected: Additional time saving of 2-3.5% over E116 (~4.15-4.22 s): group 2 is ~40% of conv FLOPs, and its backward runs over ~8% of samples, all at 32 px. Extra accuracy loss 0.03-0.10 pp. If the extra loss is <= 0.06 pp (<= 0.025 pp per 1%), the deeper freeze is the best measured exchange rate, and a combined schedule (group 1 at 85%, group 2 at 92%) becomes the next tip candidate once funded. If the loss is >= 0.1 pp, the late-freeze depth is capped at group 1.
description: Deeper late freeze. Base: E116 code (stem + group 1 detached from 85%). Change only one thing: from 92% of samples, also detach group 2's output, so there is no backward into stem, group 1 or group 2, and group-2 filters/BN params drop out of the Muon stacks and the SGD foreach. Add this as a third static 32 px / bs-1024 graph variant plus a matching Muon-update variant. Warm every renorm x freeze-level combination in build, and verify with TORCH_LOGS=recompiles on a 2-trial dev run. Accuracy is decided untimed on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process against the E116 large-seed vector, pooled with the I_a extension if it has run. Add one scored sample, and a second only if the loss is <= 0.06 pp.

expected: Time within ±0.5%. Central estimate -0.10 to +0.05 pp, a low prior: E008 showed more augmentation hurts at ~8 epochs, and airbench uses translate 4 only in 37-40-epoch recipes. A gain of >= +0.08 pp (~2.5 SE) would be a zero-time accuracy source that funds the 85% freeze outright, reopening augmentation strength under Muon (Cutout, late-phase only). A result of <= -0.08 pp confirms the short budget under-fits under Muon too and closes H12.3.
description: Augmentation strength under Muon. Base: E100 code. In the 28 and 32 px phases only, raise the translate magnitude from 2 to 4 px (same reflect padding and the same fused GPU op; the pad width is a host-side constant per phase). If the augment op is compiled, warm both pad variants in build. The 16/24 px phases, flip, LS and everything else stay unchanged. Smoke-test that one batch of translated images is in range and shape-correct. Decide untimed on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process against the pooled 200-trajectory E100 baseline. Add one scored sample, and a second only if the gain is >= +0.05 pp.

expected: Time -2.0 to -2.5% vs the 4.26 s tip (about 4.15-4.18 s), from ~90 fewer 32/28 px steps at ~1.7 ms each. E121 (99 seeds) found extra updates worth +0.004 pp, so my central accuracy estimate is -0.03 ± 0.04 pp (population mean ~0.7515-0.7522). Bankable only if the paired loss is <= 0.03 pp and the arm mean is >= 0.7518. A further 100 seeds then confirm before banking under H4.9. If the loss is 0.03-0.08 pp, it becomes a funded candidate, to be paired with whichever accuracy source lands. If the loss is >= 0.1 pp, the bs-1024 tail was a real purchase despite E121, and H2.11 closes.
description: Revert the tip's bs-1024 late phases. Base: E116 code (82e6219). Precondition, free (H4.2.4): log the source hash and a one-line diff against 82e6219. Change only the batch size of the 28 px and 32 px phases, from 1024 to 1536. Keep the sample-indexed schedule (LR warmup/decay, floor-hold, renorm cadence and the 85% freeze point all in samples). Rescale the SGD groups (BN biases, whitening bias, head bias) in those phases by the kilostep rule. Keep the Muon lr x1.25 at 32 px and momentum 0.6. Keep the final-EMA window and lookahead stop pinned to the last 8 steps. Compile static bs-1536 28/32 px graphs and warm every freeze x renorm x whiten-bias-grad variant for the new shapes in build. Verify on a 2-trial dev run with TORCH_LOGS=recompiles that nothing compiles after build. Accuracy is decided untimed through the benchmark trial code on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process, against the pooled ~198-trajectory E116 baseline (SE ~0.032). Add one scored run with per-trial prepare/train logs to measure the real time.

expected: Projected time -6.5 to -7.5% (about 3.95-4.0 s); slightly less than E123's 7.6% because the freeze already removes group-1 backward over the last 15%. My central accuracy estimate is -0.15 to -0.35 pp (capacity on the 31x31 maps; SGD-era capacity cuts cost ~0.1 pp per 1%). If the loss is <= ~0.25 pp (<= 0.035 pp per 1%, judged against the slope that the H2.10.6 arms measure), queue a funded variant that re-spends ~half the saving on 32 px epochs to restore mu >= 0.7521, for a net ~-3 to -4%. If the loss is >= 0.4 pp, this cut is worse than the slope.
description: Depth cut arm (a), 2/3/3. Base: E116 code. Remove group-1 conv3 (with its BN and GELU) so group 1 is conv1 plus a single-conv residual branch. Re-batch the Muon filter stacks for the changed counts, including the frozen-group-1 update variant. Rebuild the dirac init over the remaining convs. Warm every (resolution, batch) x freeze x renorm x whiten-bias-grad variant in build, and check on a 2-trial dev run with TORCH_LOGS=recompiles that nothing compiles after build. Change nothing else: schedule, 85% freeze, tail. Before deciding, run an untimed per-step profile of the modified net at all four shapes (with the frozen 32 px variant) and project total time over the E116 schedule, because E123's -7.6% was measured with the freeze off. Accuracy is decided untimed on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process against the pooled ~198-trajectory E116 baseline. Score once only if the loss is <= 0.35 pp.

expected: Time per arm about ±0.11 s (±2.5%). Accuracy: A about -0.08 to -0.20 pp, B about +0.05 to +0.15 pp, i.e. a slope of 0.03-0.07 pp per 1%, resolved to ±0.035 pp per arm. This rate is the bar for the depth cuts, group-3 width 512, the bs-1536 revert and 12 px swaps, and it sizes how many re-spent 32 px samples a depth cut must buy back. If B gains >= 0.1 pp, re-spending into 32 px is an efficient funding source. If B gains <= 0.03, the slope is concave above the tip and funded cuts must come from elsewhere.
description: Measure the local yardstick on the tip. Base: E116 code. Two untimed arms through the benchmark trial code, each on seeds 3-102 in its own fresh process: (A) 32 px phase -0.25 epoch (2.5 instead of 2.75), (B) 32 px phase +0.25 epoch (3.0). Index everything by samples (LR warmup/decay, floor-hold, renorm cadence, Muon x1.25 phase factor). Keep the freeze at 85% of the new total samples and the final-EMA/lookahead window pinned to the last 8 steps. All shapes are already static and warmed. Compare each arm with the pooled ~198-trajectory E116 baseline. For the scored row, rerun the E116 tip unchanged, which adds another distinct gate sample (H4.9.1).

expected: Time equal to the tip (±0.3%). Accuracy +0.02 to +0.06 pp over E116, recovering part of the ~0.09 pp freeze cost by removing the hard switch at a nonzero LR. A gain of >= +0.064 pp (2 SE) makes it a zero-time margin source that restores mu to ~E100's level. That would fund the bs-1536 revert or let the freeze move to ~80%. A result within ±0.03 pp means the freeze cost is lost late adaptation, not the discontinuity, and arm (b) (BN eval in the frozen window) becomes the only remaining refinement.
description: FreezeOut-style anneal before the 85% freeze, arm (a) only. Base: E116 code. Over 75%-85% of samples, ramp the LR multiplier of the group-1 filters (Muon) and the stem/group-1 BN params (SGD) linearly from 1 to 0, then detach at 85% exactly as now. Use separate 0-d LR tensors for the group-1 Muon stack and the group-1 SGD group, written host-side so nothing recompiles; if the group-1 filters currently share a stacked Muon update with others, scale their slice by a 0-d per-stack factor. All other groups, the schedule and the tail are unchanged. Time is unchanged. Accuracy is decided untimed on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process against the pooled ~198-trajectory E116 baseline.

expected: Projected time -5.5 to -6.5% (about 4.0-4.03 s); the group-3 backward is untouched by the group-1 freeze, so most of E123's -6.1% should survive. Accuracy is a low prior: -0.2 to -0.45 pp, because late capacity was valuable on CIFAR-100 (E005, and futurebiohackers chose 576 for this). If its loss per 1% is lower than arm (a)'s and <= the H2.10.6 slope, it becomes the depth-cut candidate for a funded re-spend. If both arms lose >= 1.5x their slope equivalent, depth cuts close.
description: Depth cut arm (b), 3/3/2. Base: E116 code. Remove group-3 conv3 (with its BN and GELU) so group 3 is conv1 plus a single-conv residual branch. Re-batch the Muon stacks, rebuild the dirac init, warm every shape x freeze x renorm variant in build, and check with a TORCH_LOGS=recompiles dev run. Change nothing else. Run an untimed per-step profile with the freeze on and project total time over the E116 schedule. Accuracy is decided untimed on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process against the pooled E116 baseline. Run this after arm (a), so that if both arms qualify they can be compared at equal projected saving.

expected: Time -0.3 to -0.5% (about 4.24-4.25 s; E092 saved 0.4%). H9.2 predicts a loss of >= 0.1 pp; my central estimate is -0.05 to -0.15 pp, since E092's -0.18 was 8 seeds (~1.4 SE) and regresses toward zero. If the loss is >= 0.1 pp, lookahead is real smoothing, and the H9.2.1 strength arms (ramp exponent, peak decay, final-EMA lerp) get queued as zero-time accuracy sources. If the loss is <= 0.04 pp, H9.2 closes; the ~0.4% is banked only together with an accuracy source, because the margin is gone.
description: Lookahead removal re-measured on the large-seed instrument, which gates H9.2.1. Base: E116 code. Remove the lookahead-EMA entirely: the net trains on its own weights; its buffers and foreach kernels are dropped from build and the step loop. Keep the floor-hold, the final 8-step EMA (lerp 0.3 every 4 steps), eval on the EMA weights with BN buffers from the net, and the 85% freeze. Change nothing else. Accuracy is decided untimed on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process against the pooled ~198-trajectory E116 baseline. Add one scored run with per-trial logs, because the expected time saving is inside single-run noise.

expected: Time about -3% (~4.13 s; a bs-1536 16 px epoch costs ~0.26 s, so half an epoch is ~0.13 s). Accuracy: the H8 threshold view predicts ≤0.05 pp loss. My central estimate is -0.03 to -0.10 pp, because E072/E114 suggest half a 16 px epoch might be worth ~0.1 pp. A loss ≤0.05 pp (≤0.017 pp per 1%) makes it the best measured lever: population mean ≥0.7516 stays above the 0.7513 floor, so it can be banked under H4.9 and enters the H2.23.1 combination. A loss ≥0.15 pp (≥0.05 pp per 1%) refutes the threshold view for 16 px exposure and closes low-res trims.
description: Trim the 16 px phase on the tip. Base: E116 code (82e6219). Precondition, free: log the source hash and a one-line diff against 82e6219. Change only the schedule, from 2@16 + 1.25@24 + 1.25@28 + 2.75@32 to 1.5@16 + 1.25@24 + 1.25@28 + 2.75@32 (6.75 epochs), with switches indexed by samples. Rescale LR warmup/decay, the floor-hold and the renorm cadence to the new total, as the earlier trims (E070/E088) did. Two anchors stay where they are instead of being rescaled: (a) the whitening-bias detach keeps its position inside the 24 px phase, ~0.97 epoch after the 24 px switch. Plain 41% rescaling would push it into the 28 px phase, where the grad variant is not warmed. (b) The stem + group-1 freeze keeps the same number of frozen samples before the end (~1.09 epochs), so the time saving comes only from the 16 px trim. The final-EMA/lookahead window stays pinned to the last 8 steps. All shapes and variants are already warmed; check with TORCH_LOGS=recompiles on a 2-trial dev run. Accuracy is decided untimed on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process against the pooled ~198-trajectory E116 baseline (SE ~0.032). Add one scored run with per-trial prepare/train logs.

expected: Time about -1.5% vs the tip (~4.19-4.20 s): ~0.36 more frozen epochs at ~0.19 s saved per frozen epoch, the rate E116 measured. Accuracy -0.03 to -0.10 pp vs E116 (extrapolating 92%: -0.02, 85%: -0.09 vs E100), i.e. a marginal 0.02-0.065 pp per 1%. At ≤0.05 pp per 1% (loss ≤0.08 pp) the 80% point beats 32 px re-spend and joins the H2.23.1 candidate. Above 0.06 pp per 1%, the freeze stays at 85% and the dose-response is convex.
description: Dose-response of the stem + group-1 freeze at 80% of samples. Base: E116 code. Precondition, free: source hash plus a diff against 82e6219. Change only the freeze point, from 85% to 80% of samples. It stays inside the 32 px / bs-1024 phase, which starts at ~62%. Every freeze x renorm graph and Muon-stack variant is reused unchanged from E116 (already warmed); confirm no recompiles on a 2-trial TORCH_LOGS=recompiles dev run. Accuracy is decided untimed on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process against the pooled ~198-trajectory E116 baseline. Add one scored run with per-trial logs to measure the real saving. Run a 75% arm only if the 85->80 marginal rate comes in at ≤0.04 pp per 1%.

expected: Time -1.0 to -1.5% (~4.20-4.22 s): ~27 fewer low-res steps at ~2 ms each. The H8 early-threshold view (E121: +0.004 pp for extra early steps) predicts a loss ≤0.03 pp, i.e. ≤0.025 pp per 1%, cheaper than the yardstick. That would make it a stackable component for the H2.23.1 combination. A loss ≥0.1 pp means large early batches hurt through a channel other than update count (the SGD-bias LR under the kilostep rescale, say), and early batch size closes.
description: Early bs 2048 with the warmup fixed in steps. Base: E116 code. Run the 16 px and 24 px phases at bs 2048 instead of 1536. Keep the LR warmup at the tip's step count, not its sample count, which removes E043's warmup confound. Decay, floor-hold, renorm cadence, whitening-bias detach (~41%) and the 85% freeze stay sample-indexed. Scale the SGD groups (BN biases, whitening bias, head bias) in those phases by the kilostep rule; Muon lr and momentum are unchanged. The 28/32 px phases and the tail are untouched. Compile static bs-2048 16/24 px graphs plus both whiten-bias-grad variants, warm them in build, and verify no recompiles on a 2-trial dev run. Accuracy is decided untimed on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process against the pooled E116 baseline. Add one scored run with per-trial logs.

expected: Step 1: H2.21.3 is supported if the measured detached saving is within ±3 pp of the FLOP fraction, and H2.21's bytes claim survives if it is ≥1.2x. Step 2: time -0.2 to -0.5% (~4.24-4.25 s), from dropping the batch-stat reductions over the 31x31x128 maps during ~15% of samples. Accuracy within ±0.03 pp. Train/eval BN consistency for the frozen layers may even give a small gain. If the loss is ≥0.05 pp, train-mode BN in the frozen layers still adapts usefully and the line closes. If the gain is in-noise but the time drop holds, bank it as a free component of the next combination.
description: FreezeOut arm (b), with H2.21.3's measurement done in the same step. Base: E116 code. Step 1, untimed: on the 32 px / bs-1024 shape, time with CUDA events and NVML energy over 20 steps each (i) the full graph, (ii) the current detached graph and (iii) a new detached graph in which stem + group-1 BN run in eval mode on the running stats frozen at the freeze point. Log the measured (ii)/(i) saving next to the recounted removed-FLOP fraction including group-2 conv1's dgrad (~18.5%); this settles H2.21.3. Step 2: use variant (iii) for the frozen window (85% onward), as a warmed static graph for every renorm x freeze combination. Running stats stop updating, and eval uses the same stats. Verify no recompiles on a dev run. Accuracy is decided untimed on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process against the pooled E116 baseline. Add one scored run.

expected: Projected time -4.5 to -5.5% (~4.03-4.07 s). The freeze leaves group-3 backward untouched, so most of E117's saving should survive. Accuracy -0.12 to -0.30 pp (low prior: futurebiohackers chose 576 for late capacity, and E005 agrees). A loss ≤0.18 pp (≤0.035 pp per 1%) beats the yardstick and becomes a funded candidate: re-spend ~0.15 epoch at 32 px for a net of about -2.5%. A loss ≥0.26 pp trades no better than a 32 px trim, and group-3 width closes.
description: Group-3 width 512 as a FLOP lever on the tip. Base: E116 code. Set group-3 width from 576 to 512. Group-3 conv1 input stays 384 and the head becomes [100, 512]. Re-batch the Muon stacks and the dirac init. Warm every (resolution, batch) x freeze x renorm x whiten-bias-grad variant in build, and confirm no recompiles on a 2-trial dev run. Untimed first: a per-step profile with the freeze on, projecting total time over the E116 schedule (E117 projected -5.2% with the freeze off). Accuracy is decided untimed on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process against the pooled E116 baseline. Run this after I139 (3/3/2) reports, and skip it if 3/3/2 loses ≥0.45 pp, since group-3 capacity would then be too valuable. Add one scored run only if the loss is ≤0.26 pp.
note: ideate: Its own gate fails. I145 said to skip if 3/3/2 lost ≥0.45 pp, and E130 (3/3/2) lost 0.48 pp, so group-3 capacity is too valuable. E005 and the futurebiohackers sweep also favour 576. Prior for group-3 width 512 is too low to spend a run.

expected: Time +2.5 to +4% (~4.37-4.43 s), from ~+65 late steps at ~1.7-2 ms each plus some small-GEMM inefficiency. If E126's -0.18 pp is symmetric and comes from update count, the gain is +0.08 to +0.15 pp (central +0.10), i.e. ~0.03-0.05 pp per 1%. At ≥0.06 pp per 1% it is a funding source that beats 32 px re-spend (0.05) and pairs with the freeze or the 16 px trim. At ≤0.03 pp the late-update effect saturates at bs 1024 (concave), and H11.2's update-count reading weakens.
description: Late update count, mirror of E126. Base: E116 code. Step 1, untimed: profile ms/step and NVML energy for static bs-768 graphs at 28 and 32 px, with the freeze and renorm variants. bs 768 at 32 px is ~2.5 waves on 108 SMs, so GEMM efficiency may fall. Project total time. Step 2, only if the projected cost is ≤+4%: run the 28 and 32 px phases at bs 768 instead of 1024, sample-indexed (LR, floor-hold, renorm, the 85% freeze and the Muon x1.25 at 32 px all in samples). Kilostep-scale the SGD groups; Muon lr and momentum are unchanged. Pin the final-EMA window and lookahead stop to the last 8 steps. Warm every variant and verify no recompiles. Accuracy is decided untimed on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process against the pooled E116 baseline. Add one scored run.

expected: Time about -2.1% (~4.17 s, as E126). Under the update-count mechanism (H11.2) the loss is ≥0.12 pp, reproducing most of E126's -0.18; my central estimate is -0.08 to -0.15 pp. If the loss is ≤0.05 pp (population ≥0.7516, above the 0.7513 floor), E126's cost came from the SGD rescale or the EMA window. Bank it under H4.9 as a -2.1% lever at ~0.02 pp per 1%; I146 (bs 768 late) then loses its basis and should be dropped. If the loss is ≥0.12 pp, update count is confirmed, late batch size stays closed, and I146 becomes the live H11 test.
description: Confound ablation of E126, which may also turn up a -2% time lever. Base: E116 code (82e6219). Precondition, free: log the source hash and a diff against 82e6219. Run the 28 and 32 px phases at bs 1536 instead of 1024, with two differences from E126: (1) the SGD groups (BN biases, whitening bias, head bias) keep their bs-1024 per-step values in those phases, with no kilostep rescale; (2) the final-EMA window and the lookahead stop are pinned to the tip's sample count (~8192 samples, i.e. the last ~5 steps at bs 1536, final EMA ~2 updates spaced to cover the same samples). LR warmup/decay, the floor-hold, the renorm cadence, the 85% freeze and Muon x1.25 at 32 px stay sample-indexed; Muon lr and momentum are unchanged. Reuse E126's warmed bs-1536 28/32 px graphs (every freeze x renorm variant) and verify no recompiles on a 2-trial TORCH_LOGS=recompiles dev run. Accuracy is decided untimed on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process against the pooled ~198-trajectory E116 baseline (SE ~0.032), with an E126 same-seed comparison. Add one scored run with per-trial logs.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.3%). Augmentation response is steep (translate 4: -0.56 pp, E131), and the run is under-trained at ~1 pp per 32 px epoch, so weaker late augmentation may help. My central estimate is -0.05 to +0.10 pp. A gain of ≥+0.08 pp (~2.5 SE) restores margin (population ~0.7529), which funds a ~1.5% 32 px trim at the 0.054 pp per 1% rate. Then queue translate 0 and a combined trim. A loss of ≥0.05 pp means translate 2 is at the optimum and augmentation strength closes in both directions.
description: Weaker late augmentation. Base: E116 code. In the 28 and 32 px phases only, reduce the translate magnitude from 2 to 1 px. Keep the same reflect-pad fused GPU op with the pad width as a host-side per-phase constant, and keep the alternating flip. The 16/24 px phases, LS, the schedule, the freeze and the tail are unchanged. If the augment op is compiled, warm the pad-1 variant in build and check on a 2-trial dev run that nothing recompiles. Smoke-test one batch for range and shape. Accuracy is decided untimed on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process against the pooled E116 baseline. Add one scored run. Translate 0 is a follow-up only if translate 1 gains ≥+0.04 pp.

expected: Time unchanged. Central estimate -0.08 to +0.10 pp. A gain of ≥+0.08 pp gives zero-time margin worth ~1.5% of time through a 32 px trim, and LS 0.15 becomes the next arm. A result within ±0.05 pp closes LS at population level (E009/E037/E078 then all agree). A loss of ≥0.08 pp means the target-side regularization binds even more than under SGD.
description: Re-screen label smoothing at population level under Muon. Base: E116 code. Change only the label-smoothing constant from 0.3 to 0.2, a loss constant inside the compiled train graph. Re-warm the graphs in build if the constant is baked in, and verify no recompiles on a dev run. Nothing else changes. Accuracy is decided untimed on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process against the pooled E116 baseline. Add one scored run. E037 (LS 0.2, 3 seeds, SE ~0.2 pp) could not exclude ±0.3 pp; tuned Muon CIFAR recipes use LS ~0.09.

expected: Time unchanged. Under Muon the filters are renormed and orthogonally updated, so the 64x BN-bias LR may now add noise, since it was sized for SGD lr 9 dynamics. Central estimate -0.05 to +0.10 pp. A gain of ≥+0.08 pp is a margin source, with 16x as the next arm. A loss of ≥0.08 pp means the BN biases carry fast adaptation (consistent with E051's warmup sensitivity); then 96x is worth one arm. A result within ±0.05 pp closes the bias multiplier.
description: The SGD multiplier on the BN biases was inherited from the SGD era and never re-tested under Muon. Base: E116 code. Change only the LR multiplier of the BN-bias SGD group from 64x to 32x, through its 0-d LR tensor or a host constant so nothing recompiles. The whitening-stem bias (E093 showed it is fragile), the head bias, the warmup and the Muon groups are unchanged. Accuracy is decided untimed on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process against the pooled E116 baseline. Add one scored run.

expected: Projection: (a) saves ~10-14% (stem + group 1 hold ~31% of 32 px backward, E122, plus forward and BN/GELU bytes on the largest maps); (b) saves ~5-7%; (c) saves ~14-18%. Accuracy has a low-to-moderate prior. Early high-resolution capacity was fragile (E093, E032), but group-1 conv3 removal traded at only ~0.04 pp per 1% (E127). Central estimate for (a): -0.3 to -0.6 pp, i.e. 0.03-0.05 pp per 1%. A rate ≤0.044 pp per 1% would be the first lever to move the frontier (H14), funded by re-spending ~half the saving on 32 px for a net ~-4 to -6%. If no variant projects ≥8%, structural early-stage changes close with no accuracy run.
description: Structural early-stage redesign, profiled untimed before any accuracy run. Base: E116 code. Build three variants in a side script: (a) group 1's max-pool moved from after conv3 to after conv1, so the residual conv2/conv3 run at 15x15x128 instead of 31x31x128; (b) group-1 width 96 instead of 128, with group-2 conv1 input 96 and Muon stacks plus dirac init re-batched; (c) both. Compile and warm every (resolution, batch) x freeze x renorm x whiten-bias-grad shape. Measure ms/step and NVML energy over 20 steps per shape (16/24 px bs 1536, 28/32 px bs 1024, frozen 32 px variant), and project total time over the E116 schedule. Score at 100 seeds against the pooled E116 baseline only the variants projecting ≥8% saving, best projected first. Bar: loss ≤0.044 pp per 1% (fundable by 32 px re-spend). For the scored row, rerun E116 unchanged unless a variant qualifies.

expected: Time about -3% (~4.13 s, as E132). Frontier prediction (H14): loss ≥0.12 pp (≥0.04 pp per 1%), similar to E132's -0.17. If the loss is ≤0.05 pp, E132's cost was a rescale artifact (warmup and decay compression), and the 16 px trim reopens as a ~0.015 pp per 1% lever that keeps the population ≥0.7513 and is bankable under H4.9. H8.3 would then be marked a confounded refutation.
description: Clean 16 px trim that separates trim value from schedule-rescale artifacts. Base: E116 code. Drop only the first 0.5 epoch of the 16 px phase: start the sample-indexed schedule at 0.5 epoch in, so every later event keeps its absolute sample position (LR decay, floor-hold, renorm cadence, whitening-bias detach, 85% freeze, 24/28/32 px switches). The LR warmup is kept in steps from the new start. Total samples 6.75 epochs. All shapes are already warmed; verify no recompiles on a 2-trial dev run. Accuracy is decided untimed on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process against the pooled E116 baseline, same base, and compared with E132's rescaled trim on the same seeds. Add one scored run.
